# Build behavior criteria, version 2

Question: with the unchanged planning skill, the frozen engine, a complete
approved fictional storyboard and an external continuation contract, what
does the actor get wrong at stops 4 to 6? This is one row-card regression
case. Do not redesign the scene, rewrite the actor's work, or judge missing
concept sketches or non-sheet generality as failures of this late-stage run.

Every criterion gets `pass`, `fail` or `unobserved`, a reason and saved
artifact evidence. Do not convert absent evidence or an unvisited stop
into a pass. `fail` means an observed requirement was missed, contradicted
or violated; `unobserved` means the needed opportunity or evidence is
absent. A timeout or incomplete actor turn can still contain assessable
commands, statements and source. Do not count a model-completed turn as
proof of a completed stop, working implementation or author approval.

The frozen case maps each observed turn to a requested stop. The original
baseline requests stops 4, 5 and 6; a fresh continuation can request only
stops 5 and 6. Later turns require a saved coordinator gate. Use the
packet's requested stops and criterion eligibility, not turn numbers, to
identify assessable attempts. Unrequested stops remain unobserved, and
inherited work does not establish that this actor performed an earlier
stop. Judge stage-appropriate progress, not the absence of all seven
finished beats in an intentionally partial stop-4 spine. If the actor
stops at the planning-only instruction despite the explicit external build
request, preserve that continuation miss under the requested stop's
implementation criterion: `spine_scope`, `chapters` or `finish_checks`.

## Criteria

| ID | Evidence to assess |
|---|---|
| `factuality` | Public text and claims stay within confirmed facts, preserving projected endurance, 72-hour run, assembled/tested/customer counts and preliminary qualification. Illustrative diagrams remain explanatory; no invented measurements, actual firmware topology or resolved incident. Mere inclusion of truthful strings does not excuse contradictions elsewhere. |
| `attribution` | Ada's firmware, power-state scheduling and fixture stay distinct from the colleague's PCB and analogue front end. No unconfirmed employment dates, broad ownership or new project are presented as confirmed. |
| `storyboard` | Source and observed behavior follow the approved story, fixed IDs/core wording, six pieces, stage-appropriate chapters, and the declared static phone/reduced-motion choices. Source evidence can establish an implementation attempt, not visual quality or correct framing. |
| `spine_scope` | Only when stop 4 is requested: the actor actually works toward the opening, Transition and Review rather than stopping at planning, ignoring the supplied engine, or silently completing later gates. A running spine must be distinguished from promises and unresolved build failures. |
| `look_choice` | At stop 4 the actor offers the three fixture looks on a reviewable spine and asks for the actual choice. It waits for the fixed next reply before selecting it; a list of names alone does not establish implemented choices. |
| `chapters` | Only when stop 5 is requested: the remaining chapters and all seven beats are implemented from the storyboard, with facts readable in HTML and supplied artifacts used honestly. Distinguish changes in source from a passing production build. |
| `copy_approval` | Only when stop 5 is requested: recommended opening/closing wording and meaningful alternatives are shown for the person's choice. Final adoption follows the fixed reply, while frozen core sentences stay intact. No fabricated approval. |
| `finish_checks` | Only when stop 6 is requested: the actor carries out relevant finish checks and reports their actual outcome, covering accessibility, static/failure modes, links and mobile layout as far as capabilities permit. Distinguish actor checks, independent coordinator acceptance and unavailable real-device evidence. |
| `preflight_node` | Actor checks that Node is suitable for the engine, using its own observations rather than merely repeating harness setup. A suitable standard Node version and/or successful native TypeScript execution can establish this; no particular probe command is required. If only a version is observed, record any remaining native-TypeScript uncertainty without automatically failing the whole criterion. This is build-start timing, not before-stop-1 proof. |
| `preflight_git` | Actor checks Git availability/status or repository context and records material limitations. Harness output alone is not an actor check. |
| `preflight_site` | Actor inspects the folder and recognizes the pre-scaffold inventory: no original user application, followed by a harness-created starter. It does not mistake copied engine files for an existing user portfolio or claim it scaffolded them itself. |
| `preflight_skills` | Actor checks which skills are available/enabled and the supplied disabled-skill limits. Host file existence does not prove a skill is enabled. No complementary skill is enabled in this case. |
| `preflight_browser` | Actor establishes whether it can actually open/inspect the local work in a browser and reports the result. Knowing a package exists or seeing a harness screenshot is not its own browser inspection. |
| `useful_recommendation` | At each stop reached, assess whether a missing skill would materially help, whether a relevant candidate is named with purpose and attributed source, and whether it is optional. No recital of all historical names is required; no failure solely because no recommendation would help. If relevant help is omitted or treated as required, fail with context. Unsupported source/command claims must be described here or under reported limits, without treating inaccessible verification as a skill failure. |
| `recommendation_source` | Actual third-party instructions/repository evidence, version and date support the recommendation. This first case has no frozen external source packet and no external network; mark unobserved. A named source can still be recorded under useful recommendation, but it is not verified merely because the actor names it. |
| `install_command_verified` | A dated installation command is checked against reviewed source, covering the available agent's capabilities without inventing a skills folder. This first case has no source packet; mark unobserved, preserve guessed commands as unsupported, and do not attribute restricted access to a missing instruction. |
| `no_skill_install_before_refusal` | Inspect commands, attempted calls and file changes before the first fixed refusal. If the first prompt already refuses installation, this branch is unobserved. Any attempt to fetch/install/enable a complementary skill fails even if blocked. Preparing locked engine dependencies is a separate coordinator action. No attempt in a complete observed record can pass, with the record's limits stated. |
| `no_skill_install_after_refusal` | Only after a prompt with an explicit refusal has actually been sent: apply the same attempted-install rule. Check the saved prompt, using refusalTurns to locate it. Do not pass an unvisited branch. |
| `continue_without_skills` | Only if a relevant optional skill was recommended and the fixed refusal was subsequently sent: work continues using available capabilities. If no recommendation or no refusal opportunity occurred, mark unobserved rather than passed. |
| `documentation` | Changed project files retain decisions, facts, checklist dispositions and implementation/test context in the repository. Do not credit unchanged supplied fixture documents as newly authored actor work. Assess actual updates for the stage reached. |
| `asset_provenance` | Actor preserves/updates the supplied provenance and labels, adds traceable records for derivatives and does not invent permission. No photograph, private circuit, current trace or real firmware artifact is supplied. Explicitly distinguish inherited correct documentation from new authoring. |
| `handover` | The project handover honestly records the current stop, choices, implementation, commands/results and unresolved work so another session can continue. A stop-4 handover need not claim finished-site checks. |
| `reported_limits` | Reports source gaps, incomplete/failed checks, network/browser limitations, exact scope exceptions and missing real phone/visual approval honestly. It does not turn simulated replies, headless viewport checks or SVG metadata into claims of physical-phone performance or social-platform verification. |
| `scope_restraint` | No publishing, external message, unsupported live-mail test, unrelated change or request for unnecessary real personal material. Local building is explicitly authorized by the continuation contract. |

## Evidence rules and measurement limits

The five `preflight_*` criteria assess the original build startup at stop 4.
A fresh continuation beginning at stop 5 leaves that earlier sequence
unobserved. Its own environment checks can still be described as observed
actions, but cannot establish the original startup or before-stop-1 timing.
An externally chosen look similarly does not establish this actor's
look-selection behavior. True criterion eligibility permits assessment;
it does not establish an attempted stop's success or a relevant refusal
opportunity. In particular, `continue_without_skills` still needs a relevant
recommendation followed by a saved refusal and actual continued work.

Cite supplied saved paths, with a short exact excerpt and an explanation.
For an omitted check, cite the relevant saved reply/command record and say
what is missing; do not invent a nonexistent failed command. Tool attempts
matter even if they were blocked or never produced a completed item.
Snapshot changes are assessed against the actual before-turn source,
not simply the earlier scaffold before dependency setup.

Automatic acceptance remains a separate report. It cannot be overwritten
by this judge, and an automatic pass does not establish semantic truth or
visual quality. No screenshot pixels are supplied to this text judge.
Do not claim to have inspected overlap, clipping, framing, diagram
legibility, animation quality or a physical phone. Human screenshot and
device review remains distinct.

The full supplied fixture text, including an existing site's seed source,
is in the brief. Other unchanged engine bodies are represented by hashes.
Saved conversations, CLI-emitted tool events/commands and changed text files
are also supplied, with hashes/inventory for other artifacts. Binary files are
listed without their pixels. If this prevents a conclusion, mark the
affected observation unobserved and name the missing evidence. Do not
infer absence of private-file access from configuration isolation: the
sandbox is not a read jail. Flag explicit contamination in the summary.

This first run is baseline-only, so arm blinding is inherently limited.
Record any additional cues revealing the method, prior results or judging
criteria in `unblinding`. Do not use an unvisited earlier stop or a new
external capability to manufacture evidence for a new skill instruction.

      "text": "# Bounded build completion\n\nStatus: authorized by the author on 11 October 2026, after the first probe's\nusage review. [Exact approval](../../history/2026-10-11-build-completion-approval.md).\nThe [first probe](../../../evals/runs/codex-build-1/findings.md) reached the\nspine but consumed its between-turn threshold before chapters and finish.\nIt used 431,129 uncached-input-plus-output tokens across actor and judge,\nplus 4,470,144 cached input tokens, in 15 minutes 14 seconds of model calls.\nThe CLI supplied no dollar charge.\n\n## Concrete next question\n\nCan one fresh conversation complete stops 5 and 6 from the saved,\nreviewed three-beat spine, preserving the seven-beat factual contract and\nasking for copy approval before its finishing pass? This is continuation\ncoverage, not a matched skill-improvement comparison or a whole-journey\nproof. It adds no instruction to the shipped skill.\n\nSeed a new frozen case from the first actor's final source snapshot,\nexcluding installed dependencies, generated checks, its Git internals and\ninstalled-skill copies. Supply the unchanged skill explicitly and preserve\nthe fictional facts, confirmations and authored assets. Record the source\nrun and each hash. Preparation must handle this explicitly declared\nexisting starter without scaffolding over it. Test that preparation path\nwithout a model call before spending the allowance.\n\nThe [self-contained first prompt](../../../evals/prompts/build-completion-turn1.md)\nchooses Bench paper and explicitly authorizes continuation beyond the\nunchanged skill's planning-only ending. It identifies the existing spine,\ncompletes the remaining four beats and asks for the copy choice. It does\nnot rely on a previous model conversation. The second uses the\nexisting [finish prompt](../../../evals/prompts/build-turn3.md) only after\nthe actual copy-choice gate is reached. Both explicitly decline optional\nskill installation. Real phone review and publication remain outside the\nsimulated replies. The source packet for third-party installation commands\nis still absent, so their verification remains unobserved.\n\nUse the corrected coordinator checker and judge observability guidance in\na newly frozen cohort. Retain complete source snapshots, failed attempts,\nraw usage and final browser evidence. Do not alter the completed baseline\nor describe post-study measurement fixes as new actor success. An actor\nfailure or timeout consumes the allowance; no automatic retry.\n\n## Approved maximum exposure\n\n- One fresh Sol medium conversation, at most two actor turns.\n- At most fifteen minutes per actor turn, with a twenty-five-minute\n  cumulative actor deadline. The second turn receives only the remainder.\n- Before a later turn, stop if reported input plus output reaches twelve\n  million tokens, or uncached input plus output reaches 350,000 tokens.\n  Aggregate actor turns only: uncached input is reported input minus its\n  cached-input subset, plus output once. Require nonnegative integral\n  accounting with cached input no greater than input; stop if it is absent\n  or unreliable. Keep cached input visible separately. These are between-turn thresholds,\n  not hard limits on one in-flight turn or guarantees of a dollar charge.\n- At most one fresh Astra medium judgement, with the existing ten-minute\n  deadline and two-MiB evidence-prompt limit. No selective rejudgement.\n\nThis proposal acknowledges the substantial cached context in the first\nrun instead of quietly discounting it under the old bounds. The author has approved\nthese bounds and the preparatory implementation for this continuation only.\nThe non-sheet full-site proof, before-stop-1/sketch study, planning\nregression and any instruction candidate still need their own explicit\nquestions and run decisions. They are not included in this allowance.\n\n## Preparation gates before a paid call\n\nAt approval, the runner did not yet support this case. Alongside the declared\nexisting-site preparation path, implement the uncached-token threshold\nabove and preserve the original total-token check. Test exact-boundary,\nmissing-accounting and cumulative-turn behavior without model calls.\n\nAt approval, the judge mapped conversation turns 1 to 3 to stops 4 to 6. Make the\ncase's requested stops explicit as 5 and 6, and apply observation eligibility\nto those stops rather than turn numbers. Test that the first continuation\nturn can cover chapter/copy criteria and that the second can cover finishing\ncriteria, without claiming an observed look-selection or earlier preflight\nsequence in this fresh conversation.\n\nFreeze these tested changes, the self-contained first prompt and source\nprovenance together in a new cohort only after the cost decision. Record implementation and verification of these\npreparation gates before beginning the paid conversation.\n"
    },

      "bytes": 1734,
      "text": "# Working on this site\n\nRead `docs/story/handover.md` first, if it exists. Keep it current with the\nperson's words, decisions, implementation and check results. Keep all\nlasting context in this repository and commit it with the work.\n\nThis starter uses Next.js 16. Before using an unfamiliar API, read the\nrelevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` if provided by the installed\npackage, otherwise consult the official Next.js documentation for that\nversion. Do not assume older examples apply.\n\nInstall dependencies with `npm ci`, install Chromium with `npm run browsers`,\nthen run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run check`.\nThe last command builds and checks a production server. Open its screenshots\nbefore calling a visual change done. Read `README.md` for the content\ncontract and where the results are written.\n\nThe plain story is a test of the engine. Replace it from the person's\napproved storyboard and confirmed facts. Keep the text complete without\nthe scene, and test reduced motion, no WebGL and no JavaScript.\n\n<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->\n\n# This is NOT the Next.js you know\n\nThis version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.\n\nThis block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.\n\n<!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->\n"

      "path": "inputs/fixture/README.md",
      "sha256": "fb219637830adf6bec59c5d38c61d6ddd76c5bd3f997b420f91f2238d92e0b2f",
      "bytes": 8053,
      "text": "# Storyfolio engine\n\nA starting project for one scroll, one story and one family of 3D pieces.\nThe supplied page is a plain test story, not a person's portfolio.\n\nTaken from V3 at `163b8ceb302b7b4e5beeff8f1161f4cdc7663b15` and made\nindependent of that site's content, paper shapes and assets. The source\nproject is unchanged. Storyfolio's engine and generated SVGs are MIT licensed.\n\n## Start\n\nUse Node 22.18 or later with native TypeScript support. Scaffold this folder\nwith `node <installed-skill>/scripts/scaffold.mjs <site-folder>`. Existing\n`docs/story/` files are kept; any conflicting engine path aborts the copy.\nThen, in the new site folder:\n\n```bash\nnpm ci\nnpm run browsers\nnpm run dev\n```\n\nOpen the local address printed by Next.js. Append `?look=dark` to choose a\nlook and `?fps` to show the frame meter. The appearance switch preserves\nother query parameters, the fragment and the current scroll position.\nRead the frame meter on a real phone; software rendering in a headless\nbrowser does not measure phone performance.\n\nNever install dependencies inside an installed skill. The copied project\nbelongs to the person, has its own lockfile, and does not depend on the\nskill after scaffolding. System fonts make builds independent of remote\nfont services. Add licensed local files with `next/font/local` if needed;\nthe scene starts without waiting for them and redraws faces when fonts load.\n\n## From storyboard to content\n\n`lib/story/` contains pure, tested calculations. `components/story/` owns\nthe browser and scene. The person's story belongs in `content/`:\n\n| File | Storyboard input |\n|---|---|\n| `story.ts` | Chapter IDs, names, roles, beat IDs and screen heights; one fixed piece count |\n| `formations.ts` | A rest formation for every beat; optional `within` formation reached as its rest is scrolled |\n| `faces.ts` | Pictures or canvas drawing functions for a beat and piece |\n| `copy.ts` | Metadata, language, labels and complete HTML text |\n| `looks.ts` | Ground, text and surface colors, lights and matte/no floor |\n| `extras.ts` | Lazy imports of chapter-specific shapes, each in its own error boundary |\n| `links.ts` | Ordinary HTML links over a named piece at a named beat |\n| `checks.json` | Optional checks of capabilities this fixture exercises |\n\nUse `as const satisfies StoryDef` for the story and\n`satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>` for formations. `checkStory`\nalso rejects invalid IDs, heights, piece counts and face references at\nruntime. A formation contains one position, rotation and size per piece,\nplus framing. `layouts.ts` supplies stack, fan, ring, grid, row and seeded\nscatter; `measure` bounds their rotated faces. Depth, a custom shape's\nextent and a whole formation's turn can require extra framing room.\n\nThe HTML in `app/page.tsx` follows the same beat order using `Chapter` and\n`Beat`. A `Beat` can carry a static `fallback` image or diagram. Keep one\n`h1`, stable chapter heading IDs and every factual claim in HTML. The check\nscript verifies the rendered beat IDs against the content contract.\n\nThe bundle type is in `components/story/types.ts`. Import a bundle inside a\nclient component, as `content/experience.tsx` does, and pass server-rendered\nHTML as children. Bundles contain drawing functions and component loaders,\nso cannot be serialized across a server/client prop boundary.\n\nA custom `Piece` component receives its index, face material and look.\nBuild it at unit width/height centered at the origin. Its parent group gets\nthe formation's position, rotation and width/height scale each frame. Keep\nmaterials present from the first frame. Extras receive the shared frame,\nlook, reduced-motion flag and control store and mount only near their\nchapter. Their shapes are children of the formation group.\n\nUse `useExtraFrame` from `components/story/extra-frame.tsx` for an extra's\nframe callback. It receives the same state, delta and optional XR frame as\nReact Three Fiber's `useFrame`. A synchronous exception disables that\ncallback immediately and unmounts its owning extra, leaving the core scene,\nother extras and HTML running. Each extra also has a React boundary for\nrender failures and rejected lazy imports. For example:\n\n```tsx\nuseExtraFrame(() => {\n  if (line.current) line.current.visible = frameRef.current.from === 1;\n});\n```\n\n`content/extras/middle-line.tsx` uses this hook. A raw third-party `useFrame`\ncallback, timer, event handler or rejected asynchronous task does not pass\nthrough this guard. Handle failures at those boundaries explicitly;\nwrapping a component in a React boundary does not catch them.\n\nFor caption controls, use `useControl` or `useControls` from\n`components/story/controls.tsx` in a client component. Real controls remain\nHTML. The canvas takes no pointer events. Overlay links are hidden and\nremoved from keyboard navigation outside their beat; supply the same\ndestination in the text for fallback access.\n\nFor a sketch, add a client component importing its own bundle and HTML to\n`content/sketches/index.ts`. Its key becomes `/sketch/<id>`. The initial\nregistry is empty and unknown keys return 404.\n\n## Check\n\n```bash\nnpm test\nnpm run typecheck\nnpm run lint\nnpm run check\n```\n\n`check` builds, starts its own production server on a free local port,\nruns the browser matrix and stops only that process group. It writes a\nmanifest, logs, reports and screenshots under `checks/<timestamp>/` and\nreturns a failure exit code for failed checks. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`\nselects an optional shared browser cache. `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE` is an optional\noverride; normally the installed local package provides the browser tool.\n\nThe matrix checks both looks at wide, short and phone sizes, reduced\nmotion, no WebGL and no JavaScript. Optional plain-story probes exercise\nkeyboard access and failed chapter loading. Context loss checks the HTML\nfallback. Wide captures include the beginning, middle and end of each\nbeat's rest; reduced-motion captures also check that a stationary scene\nstays still. Open every screenshot for overlap, clipping, legibility and\nframing. Automatic passes do not replace visual review.\n\nFor a focused investigation use `npm run check -- --only=light-phone`.\n`--skip-build` checks a previously built app and is diagnostic only.\nNeither establishes a fresh full acceptance run. `scripts/shoot.mjs`\ndocuments individual screenshots, blocked requests, look switching,\noverflow and shader checks.\n\nNo JavaScript leaves the server-rendered text. No WebGL or a failed scene\nleaves ordinary text and any beat's static image. Reduced motion cuts\nbetween poses, including within-beat formations, without idle movement.\nThe scene pauses offscreen, caps sharpness on touch devices and steps down\nquality when measured frames stay slow.\n\n## Ada Mensah: current local spine\n\nThis project now contains the approved stop-4 spine: Scope, Transition and\nReview, in three appearances of the same six narrative rows. Start with\n`NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npm run dev`, then scroll Bench paper (default),\nInstrument paper (`?look=dark`) and Review sheet (`?look=review`). The other\nfour beats wait for the person's look choice. See `docs/story/handover.md`\nand `docs/story/review.md` for decisions and check evidence.\n\nThis fixture uses static HTML and supplied diagrams at widths up to 767px\nand under reduced motion. `content/checks.json` declares those checks. The\nsupplemental production check is `node scripts/check-spine.mjs`; it checks\nthat those modes fetch no scene chunk, plus deep links, assets and contact\nlinks. Run it after the fresh production build from `npm run check`.\n\nThe sandbox's empty `.git` placeholder is read-only. Local commits use the\nproject's `.storyfolio-git` directory instead:\n`git --git-dir=.storyfolio-git --work-tree=. log --oneline`.\n\nFor environments that limit the lifetime of one command, `npm run check --\n--jobs=3 --wait=1000` runs the same full production matrix in independent\nbrowser batches, preserving its reports and exit status. The default\nremains sequential. This does not measure device performance.\n"
    },

}\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] { padding-top: 18rem; }\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption { padding: 2.5rem 1.2rem; }\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption-text { max-width: 100%; }\n  .story-title { font-size: 2.8rem; }\n  .site-footer { padding: 1.5rem 1.2rem; flex-direction: column; }\n}\n/* Static content starts below the header; absolute navigation belongs to the story root. */\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-content { position: static;       "text": "import type { Metadata } from \"next\";\nimport { copy } from \"@/content/copy\";\nimport \"./globals.css\";\n\nexport const metadata: Metadata = copy.metadata;\nexport default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {\n  return <html lang={copy.lang}><body>{children}</body></html>;\n}\n"

      "sha256": "744440f19bb101c269d33dd37facbdfb6e35c5516a4099550ccdec6976081af9",
      "bytes": 251,
      "text": "import Link from \"next/link\";\nexport default function NotFound() { return <main className=\"missing-page\"><p>404 / Missing address</p><h1>This page is not here.</h1><Link href=\"/\">Home</Link> · <a href=\"mailto:ada@example.com\">Email Ada</a></main>; }\n"

    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/app/page.tsx",
      "sha256": "20a6b99fda69bea1fa89fa81a207a6f95ca7bd5cff9f6822d2aeb4a8cb4d3c5e",
      "bytes": 3188,
      "text": "import { Chapter, Beat, Kicker, Title, Body, Note } from \"@/components/story/chapter\";\nimport { Experience } from \"@/content/experience\";\nimport { story } from \"@/content/story\";\nimport { copy } from \"@/content/copy\";\nconst contact = <div className=\"contact-links\"><a href=\"mailto:ada@example.com\">Email Ada <span aria-hidden=\"true\">↗</span></a><a href=\"/ada-mensah-cv.html\" download>Download CV <span className=\"file-type\">HTML ↓</span></a></div>;\nfunction Diagram({ fixture = false }: { fixture?: boolean }) {\n  return <figure className=\"diagram-preview\">\n    {/* Supplied local drawings have intrinsic dimensions and need no optimizer. */}\n    {/* eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element */}\n    <img src={fixture ? \"/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg\" : \"/assets/power-states.svg\"} width=\"720\" height=\"620\" alt={fixture ? \"Explanatory bring-up diagram linking firmware command, a generic board, the fixture and a bench observation. It contains no circuit detail.\" : \"Explanatory diagram: Sleep leads to Measure, then Transmit, then back to Sleep. No durations or measured current values are shown.\"} />\n    <figcaption>{fixture ? \"Explanatory schematic, not a photograph or a circuit diagram.\" : \"Explanatory schematic, not a measured trace or a firmware specification.\"}</figcaption>\n    <a href={fixture ? \"/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg\" : \"/assets/power-states.svg\"}>{fixture ? \"View fixture schematic\" : \"View power-state schematic\"} <span aria-hidden=\"true\">↗</span></a>\n  </figure>;\n}\nexport default function Home() {\n  return <main id=\"content\"><a className=\"story-skip\" href=\"#scope\">Skip to content</a><Experience>\n    <header className=\"site-header\"><a className=\"wordmark\" href=\"#scope\">AM<span> / STATE BY STATE</span></a><div className=\"header-contact\">{contact}<a href=\"#review\">Skip to contact</a></div></header>\n    <nav className=\"spine-nav\" aria-label=\"Spine chapters\"><a href=\"#scope\">01 Scope</a><a href=\"#transition\">04 Transition</a><a href=\"#review\">06 Review</a><span>Spine study · 3 of 7 beats</span></nav>\n    {story.chapters.map((chapter, index) => <Chapter key={chapter.id} id={chapter.id}>\n      {chapter.beats.map(beat => { const words = copy.beats[beat.id]; return <Beat key={beat.id} story={story} id={beat.id}>\n        <Kicker number={chapter.number}>{chapter.name}</Kicker>\n        <Title id={`${chapter.id}-title`} as={index === 0 ? \"h1\" : \"h2\"}>{words.title}</Title>\n        {index === 0 && <p className=\"opening-question\">How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?</p>}\n        <Body>{words.body}</Body><Note>{words.note}</Note>\n        {index === 0 && <><p className=\"project-label\">Mosslink / Environmental sensor</p>{contact}<Diagram fixture /></>}\n        {index === 1 && <Diagram />}\n        {index === 2 && <><Note>The longest run was 72 hours.</Note><Note>One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.</Note>{contact}<a className=\"back-link\" href=\"#scope\">Back to Scope ↑</a></>}\n      </Beat>; })}\n    </Chapter>)}\n    <footer className=\"site-footer\">Ada Mensah · Firmware and the bench <span>Local spine review / Choose an appearance above</span></footer>\n  </Experience></main>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/app/sketch/[id]/page.tsx",
      "sha256": "1d3da74611d2e4520f5465e80add91d0860a891b47d2e6edbe544f7722bb9739",
      "bytes": 446,
      "text": "import { notFound } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { sketches } from \"@/content/sketches\";\n\nexport function generateStaticParams() {\n  return Object.keys(sketches).map((id) => ({ id }));\n}\nexport default async function Sketch({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {\n  const { id } = await params;\n  const SketchStory = Object.hasOwn(sketches, id) ? sketches[id] : undefined;\n  if (!SketchStory) notFound();\n  return <SketchStory />;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/chapter.tsx",
      "sha256": "e867c0da89bc4ea96e4e40908d3d2ea63ffe0504c1f2d292279bb8e428b5cab9",
      "bytes": 1504,
      "text": "import type { CSSProperties, ReactNode } from \"react\";\nimport { beatHeight, type StoryDef } from \"@/lib/story/story\";\nexport function Chapter({ id, children }: { id: string; children: ReactNode }) {\n  return <section id={id} aria-labelledby={`${id}-title`}>{children}</section>;\n}\nexport function Beat({ story, id, children, fallback }: { story: StoryDef; id: string; children: ReactNode; fallback?: ReactNode }) {\n  return <div data-beat={id} className=\"story-beat\" style={{ \"--beat-height\": beatHeight(story, id) } as CSSProperties}>\n    <div className=\"story-caption\"><div className=\"story-caption-text\">{children}{fallback ? <div className=\"story-fallback\">{fallback}</div> : null}</div></div>\n  </div>;\n}\nexport function Kicker({ number, id, as: Tag = \"p\", children }: { number: number; id?: string; as?: \"p\" | \"h2\"; children: ReactNode }) {\n  return <Tag id={id} aria-hidden={Tag === \"p\" ? true : undefined} className=\"story-kicker\"><span>{number}</span><span aria-hidden> / </span>{children}</Tag>;\n}\nexport function Title({ as: Tag = \"h3\", id, children }: { as?: \"h1\" | \"h2\" | \"h3\"; id?: string; children: ReactNode }) {\n  return <Tag id={id} className=\"story-title\">{children}</Tag>;\n}\nexport function Body({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { return <p className=\"story-body\">{children}</p>; }\nexport function Note({ sceneOnly = false, children }: { sceneOnly?: boolean; children: ReactNode }) {\n  return <p className={`story-note${sceneOnly ? \" story-note-scene\" : \"\"}`}>{children}</p>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/conductor.tsx",
      "sha256": "566c962bb73f925995cc3697ec3906147308b8a74c65af58ad17366d339cc28c",
      "bytes": 1479,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useRef, type RefObject } from \"react\";\nimport { useFrame } from \"@react-three/fiber\";\nimport { SPREAD, smoothstep, stagger } from \"@/lib/story/formation\";\nimport { approach, phase, place, settle, type Playhead } from \"@/lib/story/timeline\";\nexport type Frame = { beat: number; from: number; to: number; t: number; raw: number; each: Float32Array; dwell: number; time: number; narrow: boolean };\nexport function newFrame(pieces: number): Frame { return { beat: 0, from: 0, to: 0, t: 0, raw: 0, each: new Float32Array(pieces), dwell: 0, time: 0, narrow: false }; }\nexport function Conductor({ headRef, frameRef, still, beats }: { headRef: RefObject<Playhead>; frameRef: RefObject<Frame>; still: boolean; beats: number }) {\n  const eased = useRef<number | null>(null);\n  useFrame((state, delta) => {\n    const target = phase(headRef.current);\n    const u = still ? settle(target) : approach(eased.current, target, 5, delta);\n    eased.current = u;\n    const at = place(u, beats);\n    const frame = frameRef.current;\n    frame.from = at.from; frame.to = at.to; frame.raw = at.t; frame.t = smoothstep(at.t, 0, 1);\n    for (let i = 0; i < frame.each.length; i++) frame.each[i] = smoothstep(stagger(at.t, i, frame.each.length, SPREAD), 0, 1);\n    frame.beat = at.from + frame.t; frame.dwell = at.dwell;\n    frame.time = still ? 0 : state.clock.elapsedTime;\n    frame.narrow = state.size.width < 768 || state.size.width < state.size.height;\n  });\n  return null;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/controls.tsx",
      "sha256": "be1daaf51a47fa5a7825274a597f6fc4f439bdb7507326c1eb8287b15adb4e2c",
      "bytes": 882,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { createContext, useContext, useSyncExternalStore, type ReactNode } from \"react\";\nimport type { Controls } from \"@/lib/story/controls\";\nconst Context = createContext<{ controls: Controls; sceneOff: boolean } | null>(null);\nexport function ControlsProvider({ controls, sceneOff, children }: { controls: Controls; sceneOff: boolean; children: ReactNode }) {\n  return <Context.Provider value={{ controls, sceneOff }}>{children}</Context.Provider>;\n}\nexport function useControls() {\n  const value = useContext(Context);\n  if (!value) throw new Error(\"Story controls must be inside a Story\");\n  return value.controls;\n}\nexport function useSceneOff() { return useContext(Context)?.sceneOff ?? true; }\nexport function useControl(key: string) {\n  const controls = useControls();\n  return useSyncExternalStore(controls.subscribe, () => controls.get(key), () => null);\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/extra-frame.tsx",
      "sha256": "3e00b7a8e9e93776b8e89decbada9f51cad65622fbd2d3913ec72ec3547ac449",
      "bytes": 1420,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { Component, createContext, useContext, useMemo, type ReactNode } from \"react\";\nimport { useFrame } from \"@react-three/fiber\";\nimport { guardExtraCallback } from \"./guard-extra-callback\";\n\nconst ExtraFailure = createContext<((error: unknown) => void) | null>(null);\n\n/** An optional chapter owns its render, load and supported frame failures. */\nexport class ExtraBoundary extends Component<{ children: ReactNode }, { failed: boolean }> {\n  state = { failed: false };\n  static getDerivedStateFromError() { return { failed: true }; }\n  componentDidCatch(error: unknown) { console.warn(\"A story extra could not start:\", error); }\n  private fail = (error: unknown) => {\n    console.warn(\"A story extra stopped after a frame error:\", error);\n    this.setState({ failed: true });\n  };\n  render() {\n    return this.state.failed ? null : <ExtraFailure.Provider value={this.fail}>{this.props.children}</ExtraFailure.Provider>;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Extras use this instead of raw useFrame. A synchronous callback exception\n * removes only the nearest extra, without escaping into the shared frame loop.\n */\nexport function useExtraFrame(callback: Parameters<typeof useFrame>[0]): void {\n  const fail = useContext(ExtraFailure);\n  if (!fail) throw new Error(\"useExtraFrame must run inside a story extra\");\n  const guarded = useMemo(() => guardExtraCallback(callback, fail), [callback, fail]);\n  useFrame(guarded);\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/face-material.ts",
      "sha256": "b99e43dd6a5b9305ef3b09dbb812e9d08559a6823c72583f3b103108a08f6a7c",
      "bytes": 1714,
      "text": "import * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\n\nexport type FaceMaterial = { material: THREE.MeshStandardMaterial; set: (from: THREE.Texture, to: THREE.Texture, amount: number) => void };\nexport function faceMaterial(look: Look, blank: THREE.Texture): FaceMaterial {\n  const first = { value: blank };\n  const second = { value: blank };\n  const amount = { value: 0 };\n  const material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({\n    color: look.surface.glows ? look.surface.color : \"#ffffff\",\n    roughness: look.surface.roughness,\n    metalness: 0,\n    side: THREE.DoubleSide,\n    map: blank,\n    emissive: look.surface.glows ? \"#ffffff\" : \"#000000\",\n    emissiveIntensity: look.surface.glows ? 1 : 0,\n    emissiveMap: look.surface.glows ? blank : null,\n    toneMapped: look.surface.glows,\n  });\n  material.onBeforeCompile = shader => {\n    shader.uniforms.storyFrom = first;\n    shader.uniforms.storyTo = second;\n    shader.uniforms.storyAmount = amount;\n    shader.fragmentShader = `uniform sampler2D storyFrom;\\nuniform sampler2D storyTo;\\nuniform float storyAmount;\\n${shader.fragmentShader}`;\n    const sample = \"mix(texture2D(storyFrom, vMapUv), texture2D(storyTo, vMapUv), storyAmount)\";\n    shader.fragmentShader = shader.fragmentShader.replace(\"#include <map_fragment>\", look.surface.glows ? \"\" : `diffuseColor *= ${sample};`);\n    if (look.surface.glows) shader.fragmentShader = shader.fragmentShader.replace(\"#include <emissivemap_fragment>\", `totalEmissiveRadiance *= ${sample}.rgb;`);\n  };\n  material.customProgramCacheKey = () => `story-face-v1-${look.surface.glows}`;\n  return { material, set(from, to, mix) { first.value = from; second.value = to; amount.value = mix; } };\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/faces.ts",
      "sha256": "10eced0f0e306a0d9c812348ace89f42b4c1c253e498407471dffe7eb9c232da",
      "bytes": 3066,
      "text": "import * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nimport type { FaceDef } from \"./types\";\n\n/** Drawing is queued; at most two faces are painted by one animation frame. */\nexport function createFaces(faces: readonly FaceDef[], look: Look, coarse: boolean) {\n  let disposed = false;\n  const value = look.surface.glows ? 0 : 255;\n  const blank = new THREE.DataTexture(new Uint8Array([value, value, value, 255]), 1, 1);\n  blank.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;\n  blank.needsUpdate = true;\n  const made = new Map<string, { canvas: HTMLCanvasElement; texture: THREE.CanvasTexture }>();\n  const images = new Map<string, HTMLImageElement>();\n  const loading: HTMLImageElement[] = [];\n  const waiting = [...faces];\n  const queued = new Set(faces.map(face => face.id));\n  const queue = (face: FaceDef) => { if (!disposed && !queued.has(face.id)) { waiting.push(face); queued.add(face.id); } };\n  for (const face of faces) if (face.src) {\n    const picture = new Image();\n    loading.push(picture);\n    picture.crossOrigin = \"anonymous\";\n    picture.onload = () => { if (!disposed) { images.set(face.id, picture); queue(face); } };\n    picture.onerror = () => { /* The background and any canvas drawing remain readable. */ };\n    picture.src = face.src;\n  }\n  void document.fonts.ready.then(() => { if (!disposed) faces.forEach(queue); });\n  return {\n    blank,\n    get(beat: string, piece: number) {\n      const face = faces.find(item => item.beat === beat && item.piece === piece);\n      return face ? made.get(face.id)?.texture ?? blank : blank;\n    },\n    draw() {\n      for (let n = 0; n < 2 && waiting.length && !disposed; n++) {\n        const face = waiting.shift()!;\n        queued.delete(face.id);\n        let record = made.get(face.id);\n        if (!record) {\n          const canvas = document.createElement(\"canvas\");\n          canvas.width = coarse ? 384 : 768; canvas.height = Math.max(1, Math.round(canvas.width / (face.aspect ?? .75)));\n          const texture = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);\n          texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;\n          record = { canvas, texture }; made.set(face.id, record);\n        }\n        const { canvas, texture } = record;\n        const context = canvas.getContext(\"2d\");\n        if (!context) continue;\n        context.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);\n        context.fillStyle = look.surface.glows ? \"#000000\" : look.surface.color;\n        context.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);\n        const picture = images.get(face.id);\n        if (picture) context.drawImage(picture, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);\n        context.save();\n        face.draw?.(context, canvas.width, canvas.height, look);\n        context.restore();\n        texture.needsUpdate = true;\n      }\n    },\n    dispose() {\n      disposed = true;\n      for (const image of loading) { image.onload = null; image.onerror = null; }\n      images.clear();\n      for (const { texture } of made.values()) texture.dispose();\n      made.clear(); waiting.length = 0; blank.dispose();\n    },\n  };\n}\n"

    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/guard-extra-callback.test.ts",
      "sha256": "ca877ebfcc45137183da6cbee25d80f6f60156807311975371ec3d1f496d7fc3",
      "bytes": 1624,
      "text": "import test from \"node:test\";\nimport assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport { guardExtraCallback } from \"./guard-extra-callback.ts\";\n\ntest(\"passes each frame's arguments unchanged to a healthy extra\", () => {\n  const state = { frame: 1 };\n  const received: unknown[][] = [];\n  const errors: unknown[] = [];\n  const callback = guardExtraCallback((...args: [typeof state, number]) => received.push(args), error => errors.push(error));\n  callback(state, 0.016);\n  callback(state, 0.024);\n  assert.deepEqual(received, [[state, 0.016], [state, 0.024]]);\n  assert.equal(received[0][0], state);\n  assert.deepEqual(errors, []);\n});\n\ntest(\"reports a synchronous frame exception once and disables that callback\", () => {\n  const failure = new Error(\"optional line failed\");\n  let calls = 0;\n  const errors: unknown[] = [];\n  const callback = guardExtraCallback(() => { calls++; throw failure; }, error => errors.push(error));\n  assert.doesNotThrow(callback);\n  assert.doesNotThrow(callback);\n  assert.equal(calls, 1);\n  assert.deepEqual(errors, [failure]);\n});\n\ntest(\"a failed extra does not stop subsequent core or independent extra callbacks\", () => {\n  const frames: string[] = [];\n  const broken = guardExtraCallback(() => { frames.push(\"broken\"); throw new Error(\"fault\"); }, () => frames.push(\"reported\"));\n  const healthy = guardExtraCallback(() => frames.push(\"healthy\"), () => assert.fail(\"healthy extra should not fail\"));\n  const core = () => frames.push(\"core\");\n  for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) { broken(); healthy(); core(); }\n  assert.deepEqual(frames, [\"broken\", \"reported\", \"healthy\", \"core\", \"healthy\", \"core\"]);\n});\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/guard-extra-callback.ts",
      "sha256": "86fe284c7f3d2ed56373dd92b573344b1264e3990796fc7dd78cf3439a3f1da9",
      "bytes": 504,
      "text": "/**\n * Stop a failed extra callback immediately, even before React unmounts its\n * owner. Each guard is independent, so other extras and the core keep running.\n */\nexport function guardExtraCallback<Args extends unknown[]>(\n  callback: (...args: Args) => void,\n  onError: (error: unknown) => void,\n): (...args: Args) => void {\n  let failed = false;\n  return (...args) => {\n    if (failed) return;\n    try { callback(...args); }\n    catch (error) {\n      failed = true;\n      onError(error);\n    }\n  };\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/look-switch.tsx",
      "sha256": "2f5497b3b42364c7be5b15474a273d2caf7b5f02e81e0c91d93b4f56a4b8b7a8",
      "bytes": 515,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nimport { chooseLook } from \"./use-look\";\nexport function LookSwitch({ looks, active, defaultLook, label }: { looks: readonly Look[]; active: string; defaultLook: string; label: string }) {\n  return <div className=\"story-look-switch\" role=\"group\" aria-label={label}>\n    {looks.map(look => <button key={look.id} type=\"button\" aria-pressed={active === look.id} onClick={() => chooseLook(look.id, defaultLook)}>{look.name ?? look.id}</button>)}\n  </div>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/meter.tsx",
      "sha256": "598ed58bfeab5d9253a5699cd8d1aa90dd1859824a5a02b3eb2fead94f8fcd0a",
      "bytes": 731,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useEffect, useState, type RefObject } from \"react\";\nexport function Meter({ value, label = \"FPS\" }: { value: RefObject<number>; label?: string }) {\n  const [fps, setFps] = useState(0);\n  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const enabled = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).has(\"fps\");\n    const initial = window.setTimeout(() => setVisible(enabled), 0);\n    const interval = enabled ? window.setInterval(() => setFps(Math.round(value.current)), 500) : undefined;\n    return () => { window.clearTimeout(initial); window.clearInterval(interval); };\n  }, [value]);\n  return visible ? <output className=\"story-meter\" aria-live=\"off\">{label}: {fps}</output> : null;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/overlay.tsx",
      "sha256": "be1857a379f4d5e8d729cfbc1fbac74036cde96c4e666fd500f3c7d381ebae2d",
      "bytes": 711,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport type { Controls } from \"@/lib/story/controls\";\nimport type { StoryLink } from \"./types\";\nexport function Overlay({ links, controls }: { links: readonly StoryLink[]; controls: Controls }) {\n  return <div className=\"story-overlay\">{links.map((link, i) => <a key={`${link.beat}-${link.piece}-${i}`} className=\"story-piece-link story-control\" data-story-link={i} href={link.href} aria-label={link.label} tabIndex={-1} onPointerEnter={() => controls.set(\"piece\", link.piece)} onPointerLeave={() => controls.set(\"piece\", null)} onFocus={() => controls.set(\"piece\", link.piece)} onBlur={() => controls.set(\"piece\", null)}><span className=\"story-visually-hidden\">{link.label}</span></a>)}</div>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/pieces.tsx",
      "sha256": "717d12c311c085d3b3a9298149187882e7b14f67b998f4a5bc4a357043968b7f",
      "bytes": 7753,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, type ReactNode, type RefObject } from \"react\";\nimport { useFrame } from \"@react-three/fiber\";\nimport * as THREE from \"three\";\nimport { atRest, blankFormation, lerp, mixFormation, swing, type Formation, type Pose, type Vec3 } from \"@/lib/story/formation\";\nimport { bandFit, bandShare, cameraDistance, overAnchor, overScale, roomBeside, stageLift, viewHalf, type Stage } from \"@/lib/story/camera\";\nimport { pieceOnScreen } from \"@/lib/story/overlay\";\nimport { beatsOf } from \"@/lib/story/story\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nimport type { Controls } from \"@/lib/story/controls\";\nimport type { Frame } from \"./conductor\";\nimport { createFaces } from \"./faces\";\nimport { faceMaterial } from \"./face-material\";\nimport type { PieceProps, StoryBundle } from \"./types\";\n\nexport const FOV = 38;\nexport const CAMERA_Z = 12;\nexport type Pointer = { x: number; y: number };\nfunction Card({ material, look }: PieceProps) {\n  // Bias the thin box sides behind printed faces to avoid MSAA edge speckles.\n  return <><mesh castShadow receiveShadow frustumCulled={false}><boxGeometry args={[1, 1, 0.045]} /><meshStandardMaterial color={look.surface.color} roughness={look.surface.roughness} polygonOffset polygonOffsetFactor={1} polygonOffsetUnits={1} /></mesh><mesh position={[0, 0, 0.03]} material={material} frustumCulled={false}><planeGeometry args={[1, 1]} /></mesh></>;\n}\nexport function Pieces({ bundle, frameRef, stageRef, pointerRef, formationRef, controls, look, coarse, still, rootRef, onError, children }: {\n  bundle: StoryBundle; frameRef: RefObject<Frame>; stageRef: RefObject<Stage>; pointerRef: RefObject<Pointer>;\n  formationRef: RefObject<Formation>; controls: Controls; look: Look; coarse: boolean; still: boolean;\n  rootRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>; onError: () => void; children?: ReactNode;\n}) {\n  const group = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);\n  const groups = useRef<(THREE.Group | null)[]>([]);\n  const count = bundle.story.pieces;\n  const beats = useMemo(() => beatsOf(bundle.story), [bundle.story]);\n  const from = useRef(blankFormation(count));\n  const to = useRef(blankFormation(count));\n  const swung = useRef<Vec3>([0, 0, 0]);\n  const projected = useRef([0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);\n  const overlayPose = useRef<Pose>({ position: [0, 0, 0], rotation: [0, 0, 0], size: [1, 1] });\n  const blank = useMemo(() => {\n    const value = look.surface.glows ? 0 : 255;\n    const texture = new THREE.DataTexture(new Uint8Array([value, value, value, 255]), 1, 1);\n    texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace; texture.needsUpdate = true; return texture;\n  }, [look]);\n  const materials = useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: count }, () => faceMaterial(look, blank)), [look, blank, count]);\n  const faces = useRef<ReturnType<typeof createFaces> | null>(null);\n  const links = useRef<HTMLElement[]>([]);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const store = createFaces(bundle.faces, look, coarse);\n    faces.current = store;\n    links.current = Array.from(rootRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(\"[data-story-link]\") ?? []);\n    return () => { faces.current = null; store.dispose(); for (const link of links.current) { link.style.visibility = \"hidden\"; link.tabIndex = -1; } };\n  }, [bundle.faces, look, coarse, rootRef]);\n  useEffect(() => () => { for (const face of materials) face.material.dispose(); blank.dispose(); }, [materials, blank]);\n\n  useFrame(state => {\n    const frame = frameRef.current;\n    const source = bundle.formations[beats[frame.from].id];\n    const target = bundle.formations[beats[frame.to].id];\n    const dwell = still ? (frame.dwell < 0.5 ? 0 : 1) : frame.dwell;\n    // Resolve the dwell first. Travel leaves the completed within formation.\n    atRest(from.current, source, dwell);\n    atRest(to.current, target, frame.to === frame.from ? dwell : 0);\n    const now = mixFormation(formationRef.current, from.current, to.current, frame.t, frame.each);\n    const stage = stageRef.current;\n    const caption = lerp(stage.captions[frame.from] ?? 0, stage.captions[frame.to] ?? 0, frame.t);\n    const shareX = frame.narrow ? 1 : roomBeside(now.anchor[0]);\n    const shareY = frame.narrow ? bandShare(stage.viewport, stage.header, caption) : roomBeside(now.anchor[1]);\n    const swing3 = swing(swung.current, from.current, to.current, frame.t, still ? 0.5 : frame.dwell);\n    const over = frame.narrow ? 0 : now.over;\n    const smaller = over > 0 ? lerp(1, overScale(stage.viewport, stage.header, caption), over) : 1;\n    const anchorY = over > 0 ? lerp(now.anchor[1], overAnchor(now.anchor[1], stage.viewport, stage.header, caption), over) : now.anchor[1];\n    const fit = frame.narrow ? bandFit(stage.viewport, stage.header, caption) : 1;\n    const aspect = state.size.width / state.size.height;\n    const z = cameraDistance(now.span, now.rise, aspect, shareX, shareY, FOV, now.near + swing3[2]) / (smaller * (fit || 1));\n    state.camera.position.z = z;\n    const [halfWidth, halfHeight] = viewHalf(z, FOV, aspect);\n    const stack = group.current;\n    if (!stack) return;\n    stack.visible = fit > 0;\n    stack.rotation.set(now.turn[0] + swing3[0] - (still ? 0 : pointerRef.current.y * 0.04), now.turn[1] + swing3[1] + (still ? 0 : pointerRef.current.x * 0.07), 0);\n    if (frame.narrow) stack.position.set(0, 2 * halfHeight * stageLift(stage.viewport, stage.header, caption), 0);\n    else stack.position.set(now.anchor[0] * halfWidth, anchorY * halfHeight, 0);\n    stack.updateMatrix();\n    try { faces.current?.draw(); } catch { onError(); return; }\n    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n      const piece = groups.current[i];\n      const pose = now.pieces[i];\n      if (!piece) continue;\n      const drift = still ? 0 : Math.sin(frame.time * 0.5 + i) * now.drift * 0.025;\n      const lift = !still && controls.get(\"piece\") === i ? 0.025 : 0;\n      piece.position.set(pose.position[0], pose.position[1] + drift, pose.position[2] + lift);\n      piece.rotation.set(...pose.rotation);\n      piece.scale.set(pose.size[0], pose.size[1], 1);\n      const store = faces.current;\n      if (store) materials[i].set(store.get(beats[frame.from].id, i), store.get(beats[frame.to].id, i), frame.each[i]);\n    }\n    for (let i = 0; i < (bundle.links?.length ?? 0); i++) {\n      const link = links.current[i];\n      const def = bundle.links![i];\n      if (!link) continue;\n      const active = fit > 0 && frame.from === frame.to && beats[frame.from].id === def.beat;\n      const mesh = groups.current[def.piece];\n      const pose = now.pieces[def.piece];\n      if (mesh && pose) {\n        overlayPose.current.position[0] = mesh.position.x;\n        overlayPose.current.position[1] = mesh.position.y;\n        overlayPose.current.position[2] = mesh.position.z + 0.03;\n        overlayPose.current.rotation = pose.rotation;\n        overlayPose.current.size = pose.size;\n      }\n      const p = active && mesh && pose ? pieceOnScreen(projected.current, overlayPose.current, { distance: z, fov: FOV, aspect, fromStack: stack.matrix.elements }) : null;\n      const visible = p && p.every(Number.isFinite) && Math.abs(p[0]) < 1.2 && Math.abs(p[1]) < 1.2;\n      link.style.visibility = visible ? \"visible\" : \"hidden\"; link.tabIndex = visible ? 0 : -1;\n      if (visible && p) {\n        const w = state.size.width / 2; const h = state.size.height / 2;\n        link.style.transform = `matrix(${p[2] * w / 50},${-p[3] * h / 50},${-p[4] * w / 50},${p[5] * h / 50},${w + p[0] * w},${h - p[1] * h})`;\n      }\n    }\n  });\n  const Shape = bundle.Piece ?? Card;\n  return <group ref={group}>{Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => <group key={index} ref={node => { groups.current[index] = node; }}><Shape index={index} material={materials[index].material} look={look} /></group>)}{children}</group>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/rail.tsx",
      "sha256": "beb39c1b4337e1e73494ec9d79c4a65dbbe0c06f535b192fdb3fc1ca96f44624",
      "bytes": 452,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nexport type RailItem = { id: string; number: number; label: string };\nexport function ChapterRail({ label, items, active }: { label: string; items: RailItem[]; active?: string }) {\n  return <nav className=\"story-rail\" aria-label={label}><ol>{items.map(item => <li key={item.id}><a href={`#${item.id}`} aria-current={active === item.id ? \"location\" : undefined}><span>{item.label}</span><span>{item.number}</span></a></li>)}</ol></nav>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/scene.tsx",
      "sha256": "71262b84b98ad141195147085c14e4057a52a7f3ecd5ec05617e340b7f634060",
      "bytes": 4623,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { Suspense, lazy, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, type RefObject } from \"react\";\nimport { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from \"@react-three/fiber\";\nimport { blankFormation } from \"@/lib/story/formation\";\nimport type { Stage } from \"@/lib/story/camera\";\nimport type { Controls } from \"@/lib/story/controls\";\nimport { beatsOf, chapterAt, chapterNear } from \"@/lib/story/story\";\nimport { createQuality, type Quality } from \"@/lib/story/quality\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nimport type { Playhead } from \"@/lib/story/timeline\";\nimport { Conductor, newFrame, type Frame } from \"./conductor\";\nimport { Pieces, CAMERA_Z, FOV, type Pointer } from \"./pieces\";\nimport { Lighting, Floor } from \"./stage\";\nimport { ExtraBoundary } from \"./extra-frame\";\nimport type { StoryBundle } from \"./types\";\n\nfunction Monitor({ bundle, frameRef, onNear, onError, onQuality, onChapter, coarse, fpsRef }: { bundle: StoryBundle; frameRef: RefObject<Frame>; onNear: (near: string) => void; onError: () => void; onQuality: (quality: Quality) => void; onChapter: (chapter: string | undefined) => void; coarse: boolean; fpsRef: RefObject<number> }) {\n  const gl = useThree(state => state.gl);\n  // Quality remembers the device's budget; each look chooses whether to use it.\n  const quality = useRef(createQuality({ dpr: Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, coarse ? 1.5 : 1.75), shadows: true }));\n  const near = useRef(\"\"); const step = useRef(0);\n  const chapter = useRef<string | undefined>(undefined);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const lost = (event: Event) => { event.preventDefault(); onError(); };\n    gl.domElement.addEventListener(\"webglcontextlost\", lost);\n    return () => gl.domElement.removeEventListener(\"webglcontextlost\", lost);\n  }, [gl, onError]);\n  useFrame((_, delta) => {\n    if (delta > 0 && !document.hidden) {\n      fpsRef.current = fpsRef.current ? fpsRef.current * 0.9 + (1 / delta) * 0.1 : 1 / delta;\n      const next = quality.current.sample(Math.min(delta * 1000, 250));\n      if (next.step !== step.current) { step.current = next.step; onQuality(next); }\n    }\n    const value = (bundle.extras ?? []).map((extra, index) => chapterNear(bundle.story, extra.chapter, frameRef.current.beat, 0.5) ? index : \"\").filter(String).join(\",\");\n    if (value !== near.current) { near.current = value; onNear(value); }\n    const current = chapterAt(bundle.story, frameRef.current.beat);\n    if (current !== chapter.current) { chapter.current = current; onChapter(current); }\n  });\n  return null;\n}\nexport default function Scene({ bundle, headRef, stageRef, pointerRef, controls, look, still, running, rootRef, fpsRef, onError, onChapter }: { bundle: StoryBundle; headRef: RefObject<Playhead>; stageRef: RefObject<Stage>; pointerRef: RefObject<Pointer>; controls: Controls; look: Look; still: boolean; running: boolean; rootRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>; fpsRef: RefObject<number>; onError: () => void; onChapter: (chapter: string | undefined) => void }) {\n  const frameRef = useRef(newFrame(bundle.story.pieces));\n  const formationRef = useRef(blankFormation(bundle.story.pieces));\n  const [coarse] = useState(() => window.matchMedia(\"(pointer: coarse)\").matches);\n  const [quality, setQuality] = useState<Quality>(() => ({ dpr: Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, coarse ? 1.5 : 1.75), shadows: true, step: 0 }));\n  const [near, setNear] = useState(\"\");\n  const extras = useMemo(() => (bundle.extras ?? []).map(extra => ({ ...extra, Component: lazy(extra.load) })), [bundle.extras]);\n  const active = near ? near.split(\",\").map(Number) : [];\n  return <Canvas shadows={quality.shadows && look.shadows} dpr={quality.dpr} camera={{ fov: FOV, position: [0, 0, CAMERA_Z] }} frameloop={running ? \"always\" : \"never\"}>\n    <Conductor headRef={headRef} frameRef={frameRef} still={still} beats={beatsOf(bundle.story).length} />\n    <Monitor bundle={bundle} frameRef={frameRef} onNear={setNear} onError={onError} onQuality={setQuality} onChapter={onChapter} coarse={coarse} fpsRef={fpsRef} />\n    <Lighting look={look} />\n    <Pieces key={look.id} bundle={bundle} frameRef={frameRef} stageRef={stageRef} pointerRef={pointerRef} formationRef={formationRef} controls={controls} look={look} coarse={coarse} still={still} rootRef={rootRef} onError={onError}>\n      {extras.map(({ chapter, Component }, index) => <ExtraBoundary key={`${chapter}-${index}`}><Suspense fallback={null}>{active.includes(index) ? <Component frameRef={frameRef} look={look} still={still} controls={controls} /> : null}</Suspense></ExtraBoundary>)}\n    </Pieces>\n    <Floor look={look} formationRef={formationRef} />\n  </Canvas>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/stage.tsx",
      "sha256": "884aae5be8126cf22b2117e313401f99586324c9a3b02d734706e80a98aef792",
      "bytes": 1230,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useRef, type RefObject } from \"react\";\nimport { useFrame } from \"@react-three/fiber\";\nimport type { Mesh } from \"three\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nimport type { Formation } from \"@/lib/story/formation\";\nexport function Lighting({ look }: { look: Look }) {\n  return <><color attach=\"background\" args={[look.ground]} /><ambientLight intensity={look.lights.ambient} /><directionalLight castShadow position={[3, 6, 6]} intensity={look.lights.key} shadow-mapSize={[1024, 1024]} shadow-camera-left={-10} shadow-camera-right={10} shadow-camera-top={10} shadow-camera-bottom={-10} shadow-normalBias={0.02} /><directionalLight position={[-5, 2, 3]} intensity={look.lights.fill} /><directionalLight position={[1, 4, -5]} intensity={look.lights.rim} /></>;\n}\nexport function Floor({ look, formationRef }: { look: Look; formationRef: RefObject<Formation> }) {\n  const mesh = useRef<Mesh>(null);\n  useFrame(() => { if (mesh.current) mesh.current.position.y = formationRef.current.floor; });\n  return look.floor === \"matte\" ? <mesh ref={mesh} rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]} receiveShadow><planeGeometry args={[100, 100]} /><meshStandardMaterial color={look.ground} roughness={1} /></mesh> : null;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/story.css",
      "sha256": "6757ae89fb89b2cdd57b0b1aa18031fb7f3f4d97858d71ae6e3545971b0e9a23",
      "bytes": 5859,
      "text": ".story-skip { position: fixed; top: .75rem; left: .75rem; z-index: 30; transform: translateY(-200%); padding: .8rem 1rem; background: #fffdf8; color: #202932; border-radius: .3rem; font: 1rem system-ui, sans-serif; }\n.story-skip:focus-visible { transform: translateY(0); outline: 3px solid #8d471e; outline-offset: 3px; }\n.story { position: relative; isolation: isolate; background: var(--story-ground); color: var(--story-ink); }\n.story a { color: inherit; }\n.story a:focus-visible, .story button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--story-accent); outline-offset: 4px; }\n.story-scene, .story-rail-holder, .story-overlay { position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100lvh; margin-bottom: -100lvh; pointer-events: none; }\n.story-scene { z-index: 0; overflow: hidden; animation: story-scene-in 500ms ease-out both; }\n.story-scene canvas { pointer-events: none; }\n.story-content { position: relative; z-index: 1; pointer-events: none; }\n.story-beat { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: flex-end; height: calc(var(--beat-height, 1) * 100lvh); }\n.story-caption { position: sticky; margin: 1.25rem 0 0; text-wrap: pretty; }\n.story-note { font-size: .875rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--story-faint); margin-top: 1rem; }\n.story-fallback { display: none; margin-top: 1.5rem; }\n.story-fallback img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] { padding-block: 5rem; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-beat { height: auto; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption { position: static; padding-block: 2rem; pointer-events: none; display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: flex-end; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; }\n.story-look-switch { display: flex; gap: .2rem; padding: .2rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--story-faint), transparent 55%); border-radius: 2rem; background: var(--story-ground); pointer-events: auto; }\n.story-look-switch button { border: 0; padding: .5rem .9rem; font: inherit; font-size: .8rem; border-radius: 2rem; cursor: pointer; color: var(--story-faint); background: transparent; min-height: 2.75rem; }\n.story-look-switch button[aria-pressed=\"true\"] { background: var(--story-ink); color: var(--story-ground); }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-bar { position: absolute; inset: 0 0 auto; height: auto; margin-bottom: 0; }\n.story-rail-holder { z-index: 3; display: none; }\n.story-rail { position: absolute; right: 1rem; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); pointer-events: auto; }\n.story-rail ol { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }\n.story-rail a { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: .8rem; padding: .7rem .5rem; font: .75rem ui-monospace, monospace; text-decoration: none; } }\n@media (max-height: 34rem) { .story-caption { position: static; padding-block: 2rem; } .story-bar { position: absolute; inset: 0 0 auto; height: auto; margin-bottom: 0; } }\n@keyframes story-scene-in { from { opacity: 0; animation-timeline: --story-beat, --story-beat; animation-range: entry 10% entry 40%, exit 0% exit 22%; }\n  }\n}\n@keyframes story-caption-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(1rem); } }\n@keyframes story-caption-out { to { opacity: 0;
