    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/story.tsx",
      "sha256": "de8782eb09fa55083ba63e199ce217dafda6790e2c740e8a0d809fe137f1c442",
      "bytes": 6167,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, useSyncExternalStore, type CSSProperties, type ReactNode } from \"react\";\nimport dynamic from \"next/dynamic\";\nimport type { Stage } from \"@/lib/story/camera\";\nimport { createControls } from \"@/lib/story/controls\";\nimport { playhead, type BeatBox, type Playhead } from \"@/lib/story/timeline\";\nimport { useReducedMotion } from \"./use-reduced-motion\";\nimport { useWebGLSupported } from \"./use-webgl-supported\";\nimport { useLook } from \"./use-look\";\nimport { WebGLBoundary } from \"./webgl-boundary\";\nimport { LookSwitch } from \"./look-switch\";\nimport { ChapterRail } from \"./rail\";\nimport { Overlay } from \"./overlay\";\nimport { Meter } from \"./meter\";\nimport { ControlsProvider } from \"./controls\";\nimport { checkBundle } from \"./validate\";\nimport type { StoryBundle } from \"./types\";\nconst Scene = dynamic(() => import(\"./scene\"), { ssr: false });\n\nconst staticQuery = \"(max-width: 767px), (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)\";\nfunction subscribeStatic(notify: () => void) {\n  const media = window.matchMedia(staticQuery);\n  media.addEventListener(\"change\", notify);\n  return () => media.removeEventListener(\"change\", notify);\n}\nexport function Story({ bundle, children }: { bundle: StoryBundle; children: ReactNode }) {\n  const issues = useMemo(() => checkBundle(bundle), [bundle]);\n  if (issues.length) throw new Error(`Invalid story: ${issues.join(\"; \")}`);\n  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n  const headRef = useRef<Playhead>({ beat: 0, dwell: 0 });\n  const stageRef = useRef<Stage>({ viewport: 0, header: 0, captions: [] });\n  const pointerRef = useRef({ x: 0, y: 0 });\n  const fpsRef = useRef(0);\n  const [controls] = useState(createControls);\n  const staticMode = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeStatic, () => window.matchMedia(staticQuery).matches, () => true);\n  const webgl = useWebGLSupported();\n  const still = useReducedMotion();\n  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(false);\n  const [running, setRunning] = useState(true);\n  const [activeChapter, setActiveChapter] = useState<string | undefined>(bundle.story.chapters[0]?.id);\n  const onError = useCallback(() => setFailed(true), []);\n  const id = useLook(bundle.looks, bundle.defaultLook);\n  const look = bundle.looks.find(look => look.id === id) ?? bundle.looks[0];\n  const on = !staticMode && webgl === true && !failed;\n  const items = useMemo(() => bundle.story.chapters.map(chapter => ({ id: chapter.id, number: chapter.number, label: chapter.name })), [bundle.story]);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const root = rootRef.current;\n    if (!root) return;\n    let boxes: BeatBox[] = [];\n    const update = () => { headRef.current = playhead(-root.getBoundingClientRect().top, window.innerHeight, boxes); };\n    const measure = () => {\n      const origin = root.getBoundingClientRect().top;\n      const beats = Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(\"[data-beat]\"));\n      boxes = beats.map(beat => { const box = beat.getBoundingClientRect(); return { top: box.top - origin, height: box.height }; });\n      const top = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>(\"[data-story-top]\");\n      stageRef.current = { viewport: window.innerHeight, header: top ? top.offsetTop + top.offsetHeight : 0, captions: beats.map(beat => {\n        const caption = beat.querySelector<HTMLElement>(\".story-caption\");\n        const text = beat.querySelector<HTMLElement>(\".story-caption-text\");\n        return caption && text ? text.getBoundingClientRect().height + parseFloat(getComputedStyle(caption).paddingBottom) : 0;\n      }) };\n      update();\n    };\n    measure();\n    const resize = new ResizeObserver(measure);\n    resize.observe(root);\n    root.querySelectorAll(\".story-caption-text\").forEach(node => resize.observe(node));\n    let visible = true;\n    const visibility = () => setRunning(visible && !document.hidden);\n    const seen = new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => { visible = entry.isIntersecting; visibility(); });\n    seen.observe(root);\n    document.addEventListener(\"visibilitychange\", visibility);\n    window.addEventListener(\"scroll\", update, { passive: true });\n    window.addEventListener(\"resize\", measure);\n    return () => { resize.disconnect(); seen.disconnect(); window.removeEventListener(\"scroll\", update); window.removeEventListener(\"resize\", measure); document.removeEventListener(\"visibilitychange\", visibility); };\n  }, [bundle.story, on]);\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (still) { pointerRef.current = { x: 0, y: 0 }; return; }\n    const move = (event: PointerEvent) => { if (event.pointerType === \"mouse\") pointerRef.current = { x: event.clientX / window.innerWidth * 2 - 1, y: 1 - event.clientY / window.innerHeight * 2 }; };\n    window.addEventListener(\"pointermove\", move, { passive: true });\n    return () => window.removeEventListener(\"pointermove\", move);\n  }, [still]);\n  const style = { \"--story-ground\": look.ground, \"--story-ink\": look.ink, \"--story-faint\": look.faint, \"--story-accent\": look.accent } as CSSProperties;\n  return <div ref={rootRef} className=\"story\" data-scene={on ? \"on\" : \"off\"} data-look={look.id} style={style}>\n    <noscript><style>{\".story-look-switch, .story-control { display: none !important; }\"}</style></noscript>\n    {on ? <><div className=\"story-scene\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><WebGLBoundary onError={onError}><Scene bundle={bundle} headRef={headRef} stageRef={stageRef} pointerRef={pointerRef} controls={controls} look={look} still={still} running={running} rootRef={rootRef} fpsRef={fpsRef} onError={onError} onChapter={setActiveChapter} /></WebGLBoundary></div><div className=\"story-rail-holder\"><ChapterRail label={bundle.copy.railLabel} items={items} active={activeChapter} /></div><Overlay links={bundle.links ?? []} controls={controls} /></> : null}\n    {bundle.looks.length > 1 ? <div className=\"story-bar\"><div data-story-top><LookSwitch looks={bundle.looks} active={look.id} defaultLook={bundle.defaultLook ?? bundle.looks[0].id} label={bundle.copy.lookLabel} /></div></div> : null}\n    <div className=\"story-content\"><ControlsProvider controls={controls} sceneOff={!on}>{children}</ControlsProvider></div><Meter value={fpsRef} label={bundle.copy.fpsLabel} />\n  </div>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/types.ts",
      "sha256": "29e064282d8669ff55863b5ddc20fdc477877fb03d9e8b30db8d926883a0c9b9",
      "bytes": 1421,
      "text": "import type { ComponentType, RefObject } from \"react\";\nimport type { MeshStandardMaterial } from \"three\";\nimport type { BeatFormation } from \"@/lib/story/formation\";\nimport type { StoryDef } from \"@/lib/story/story\";\nimport type { Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nimport type { Controls } from \"@/lib/story/controls\";\nimport type { Frame } from \"./conductor\";\n\nexport type FaceDef = {\n  id: string;\n  beat: string;\n  piece: number;\n  src?: string;\n  /** Printed width / height; defaults to the starter portrait card ratio. */\n  aspect?: number;\n  draw?: (context: CanvasRenderingContext2D, width: number, height: number, look: Look) => void;\n};\nexport type StoryLink = { beat: string; piece: number; href: string; label: string };\n/** Frame callbacks in optional extras use useExtraFrame to contain failures. */\nexport type ExtraProps = { frameRef: RefObject<Frame>; look: Look; still: boolean; controls: Controls };\nexport type PieceProps = { index: number; material: MeshStandardMaterial; look: Look };\nexport type StoryBundle = {\n  story: StoryDef;\n  formations: Record<string, BeatFormation>;\n  faces: readonly FaceDef[];\n  looks: readonly Look[];\n  defaultLook?: string;\n  copy: { railLabel: string; lookLabel: string; fpsLabel?: string };\n  extras?: readonly { chapter: string; load: () => Promise<{ default: ComponentType<ExtraProps> }> }[];\n  links?: readonly StoryLink[];\n  Piece?: ComponentType<PieceProps>;\n};\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/use-look.ts",
      "sha256": "4b3432dc2505b2b09d9105ab826315333bff57a3e73c395252bf072473d8649e",
      "bytes": 897,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useSyncExternalStore } from \"react\";\nimport { lookFromSearch, searchWithLook, type Look } from \"@/lib/story/looks\";\nconst event = \"story-look\";\nfunction subscribe(notify: () => void) {\n  window.addEventListener(\"popstate\", notify);\n  window.addEventListener(event, notify);\n  return () => { window.removeEventListener(\"popstate\", notify); window.removeEventListener(event, notify); };\n}\nexport function useLook(looks: readonly Look[], defaultLook = looks[0].id) {\n  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => lookFromSearch(window.location.search, looks, defaultLook), () => defaultLook);\n}\nexport function chooseLook(id: string, defaultLook: string) {\n  const { pathname, search, hash } = window.location;\n  window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, \"\", `${pathname}${searchWithLook(search, id, defaultLook)}${hash}`);\n  window.dispatchEvent(new Event(event));\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/use-reduced-motion.ts",
      "sha256": "c8760d823f342e2a378096b0b313fa882b4b7e0bf40bd0be03b423d0ffe0433e",
      "bytes": 432,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useSyncExternalStore } from \"react\";\nconst query = \"(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)\";\nfunction subscribe(notify: () => void) {\n  const media = window.matchMedia(query);\n  media.addEventListener(\"change\", notify);\n  return () => media.removeEventListener(\"change\", notify);\n}\nexport function useReducedMotion() {\n  return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, () => window.matchMedia(query).matches, () => true);\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/use-webgl-supported.ts",
      "sha256": "7315e7291bdac2453251c5b67cf301f10d23a84e9309d0839c182fc07945e419",
      "bytes": 591,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { useSyncExternalStore } from \"react\";\nlet supported: boolean | undefined;\nexport function detectWebGL(): boolean {\n  if (supported !== undefined) return supported;\n  try {\n    const canvas = document.createElement(\"canvas\");\n    const gl = canvas.getContext(\"webgl2\");\n    supported = gl !== null;\n    gl?.getExtension(\"WEBGL_lose_context\")?.loseContext();\n  } catch { supported = false; }\n  return supported;\n}\nconst subscribe = () => () => {};\nexport function useWebGLSupported() {\n  return useSyncExternalStore<boolean | null>(subscribe, detectWebGL, () => null);\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/validate.test.ts",
      "sha256": "6ee648de16b8f38ebf1f3701b2658e92b0e60a76137b6db1ca54bf601038eb19",
      "bytes": 2610,
      "text": "import test from \"node:test\";\nimport assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport { blankFormation } from \"../../lib/story/formation.ts\";\nimport type { StoryBundle } from \"./types.ts\";\nimport { checkBundle } from \"./validate.ts\";\n\nfunction bundle(): StoryBundle {\n  return {\n    story: { pieces: 1, chapters: [{ id: \"opening\", number: 0, name: \"Opening\", role: \"opening\", beats: [{ id: \"opening.one\", height: 1 }] }] },\n    formations: { \"opening.one\": { rest: blankFormation(1) } },\n    faces: [{ id: \"first\", beat: \"opening.one\", piece: 0, src: \"/face.svg\" }],\n    looks: [{ id: \"light\", ground: \"#fff\", ink: \"#111\", faint: \"#555\", accent: \"#a00\", surface: { color: \"#fff\", roughness: 1, glows: false }, lights: { ambient: 1, key: 1, fill: 0, rim: 0 }, floor: \"none\", shadows: false }],\n    copy: { railLabel: \"Chapters\", lookLabel: \"Look\" },\n  };\n}\ntest(\"accepts a complete bundle without optional extras or links\", () => {\n  assert.deepEqual(checkBundle(bundle()), []);\n});\ntest(\"rejects face identities that would share or overwrite the wrong texture\", () => {\n  const value = bundle();\n  value.faces = [...value.faces, { ...value.faces[0] }];\n  const problems = checkBundle(value);\n  assert.ok(problems.includes(\"face id used twice: first\"));\n  assert.ok(problems.includes(\"two faces assigned to opening.one:0\"));\n});\ntest(\"rejects an absent look before hydration tries to read it\", () => {\n  const value = bundle();\n  value.looks = [];\n  value.defaultLook = \"missing\";\n  assert.ok(checkBundle(value).includes(\"bundle must have a look\"));\n  assert.ok(checkBundle(value).includes(\"default look is missing: missing\"));\n});\ntest(\"rejects links and extras that could never appear\", () => {\n  const value = bundle();\n  value.links = [{ beat: \"missing\", piece: 2, href: \"\", label: \"\" }];\n  value.extras = [{ chapter: \"missing\", load: async () => ({ default: () => null }) }];\n  const problems = checkBundle(value);\n  assert.ok(problems.includes(\"link names missing beat: missing\"));\n  assert.ok(problems.includes(\"link names missing piece: 2\"));\n  assert.ok(problems.includes(\"link must have a label and destination\"));\n  assert.ok(problems.includes(\"extra names missing chapter: missing\"));\n});\n\ntest(\"bounds custom face proportions before allocating a texture\", () => {\n  for (const aspect of [0, NaN, Infinity, .01, 100]) {\n    const value = bundle(); value.faces = [{ ...value.faces[0], aspect }];\n    assert.ok(checkBundle(value).some(problem => problem.includes(\"face aspect\")));\n  }\n  const value = bundle(); value.faces = [{ ...value.faces[0], aspect: 8 }];\n  assert.deepEqual(checkBundle(value), []);\n});\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/validate.ts",
      "sha256": "8b5754eed78ef77be47067649d9fdc2e34bdff48eda5e785129e2db42d4b1915",
      "bytes": 2154,
      "text": "import { beatsOf, checkStory } from \"../../lib/story/story.ts\";\nimport type { StoryBundle } from \"./types.ts\";\n\n/** Validate the parts of a bundle that are not part of the pure story data. */\nexport function checkBundle(bundle: StoryBundle): string[] {\n  const problems = checkStory(bundle.story, bundle.formations, bundle.faces);\n  const beats = new Set(beatsOf(bundle.story).map(beat => beat.id));\n  const chapters = new Set(bundle.story.chapters.map(chapter => chapter.id));\n  const unique = (ids: readonly string[], kind: string) => {\n    const seen = new Set<string>();\n    for (const id of ids) {\n      if (!id.trim()) problems.push(`${kind} id must not be empty`);\n      if (seen.has(id)) problems.push(`${kind} id used twice: ${id}`);\n      seen.add(id);\n    }\n  };\n  unique(bundle.faces.map(face => face.id), \"face\");\n  unique(bundle.looks.map(look => look.id), \"look\");\n  if (!bundle.looks.length) problems.push(\"bundle must have a look\");\n  if (bundle.defaultLook && !bundle.looks.some(look => look.id === bundle.defaultLook)) problems.push(`default look is missing: ${bundle.defaultLook}`);\n  const assigned = new Set<string>();\n  for (const face of bundle.faces) {\n    if (face.aspect !== undefined && (!Number.isFinite(face.aspect) || face.aspect < 1/16 || face.aspect > 16)) problems.push(`face aspect must be between 1/16 and 16: ${face.id}`);\n    const key = `${face.beat}:${face.piece}`;\n    if (assigned.has(key)) problems.push(`two faces assigned to ${key}`);\n    assigned.add(key);\n    if (!face.src && !face.draw) problems.push(`face has no source or drawing: ${face.id}`);\n  }\n  for (const link of bundle.links ?? []) {\n    if (!beats.has(link.beat)) problems.push(`link names missing beat: ${link.beat}`);\n    if (!Number.isInteger(link.piece) || link.piece < 0 || link.piece >= bundle.story.pieces) problems.push(`link names missing piece: ${link.piece}`);\n    if (!link.label.trim() || !link.href.trim()) problems.push(\"link must have a label and destination\");\n  }\n  for (const extra of bundle.extras ?? []) if (!chapters.has(extra.chapter)) problems.push(`extra names missing chapter: ${extra.chapter}`);\n  return problems;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/components/story/webgl-boundary.tsx",
      "sha256": "e7b1ed45a4127bfb10af9dd22de7bcc893dc4177b562dbedbd4b93f86c4af43a",
      "bytes": 476,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport { Component, type ReactNode } from \"react\";\nexport class WebGLBoundary extends Component<{ children: ReactNode; onError?: () => void }, { failed: boolean }> {\n  state = { failed: false };\n  static getDerivedStateFromError() { return { failed: true }; }\n  componentDidCatch(error: unknown) {\n    console.warn(\"A story effect could not start:\", error);\n    this.props.onError?.();\n  }\n  render() { return this.state.failed ? null : this.props.children; }\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/checks.json",

    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/copy.ts",
      "sha256": "87cfb969d607190b00b3a2d9bc76b26e1784ef885a5ca16770cb5d7fc214856d",
      "bytes": 1290,
      "text": "export const copy = {\n  lang: \"en\",\n  metadata: {\n    title: \"Ada Mensah — Firmware and the bench\",\n    description: \"Firmware, power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture: Ada Mensah's contribution to Mosslink, with the evidence limits visible.\",\n    openGraph: { title: \"Ada Mensah — Firmware and the bench\", description: \"How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?\", images: [\"/assets/share-card.svg\"] },\n  },\n  railLabel: \"Chapters\", lookLabel: \"Appearance\", fpsLabel: \"Frames per second\",\n  beats: {\n    \"scope.opening\": { title: \"Ada Mensah\", body: \"Firmware is code that controls a physical device.\", note: \"I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture.\" },\n    \"transition.diagram\": { title: \"Reading transitions\", body: \"Sleep → Measure → Transmit → Sleep. This teaching loop explains a transition between states.\", note: \"Explanatory schematic, not a measured trace or a firmware specification.\" },\n    \"review.close\": { title: \"Code beside evidence\", body: \"I connect firmware decisions to bench observations through power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture, while keeping the evidence limits visible.\", note: \"Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle.\" },\n  },\n};\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/experience.tsx",
      "sha256": "761fa21d6b32b6fa0897ade423fe3d6d699a4e3585d91023cffbbfcbcc21ed35",
      "bytes": 260,
      "text": "\"use client\";\nimport type { ReactNode } from \"react\";\nimport { Story } from \"@/components/story/story\";\nimport { bundle } from \"./index\";\nexport function Experience({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  return <Story bundle={bundle}>{children}</Story>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/extras.ts",
      "sha256": "6c738050d7a8fc2e6bb214a401994e6a69ade3c052a263f45749699ffc5fc454",
      "bytes": 26,
      "text": "export const extras = [];\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/extras/middle-line.tsx",
      "sha256": "c0b8fe1a85bb8d66f1f8f27287b431cfdbbdcdf3bc2cb897a810dbe3c1da343c",
      "bytes": 613,
      "text": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useRef } from \"react\";\nimport { useExtraFrame } from \"@/components/story/extra-frame\";\nimport type { Mesh } from \"three\";\nimport type { ExtraProps } from \"@/components/story/types\";\n\nexport default function MiddleLine({ frameRef, look }: ExtraProps) {\n  const lineRef = useRef<Mesh>(null);\n  useExtraFrame(() => {\n    if (lineRef.current) lineRef.current.visible = frameRef.current.from === 1 && frameRef.current.to === 1;\n  });\n  return <mesh ref={lineRef} position={[0, -1.6, 0]}>\n    <boxGeometry args={[3.0, 0.025, 0.025]} />\n    <meshBasicMaterial color={look.accent} />\n  </mesh>;\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/faces.ts",
      "sha256": "28249baf7550bb8cfdfe4a8668806ccda6a94fdeb811a3d3c9be58cf91598811",
      "bytes": 1426,
      "text": "import type { FaceDef } from \"@/components/story/types\";\nimport { story } from \"./story\";\nconst table = [\"Scope / Firmware\", \"Responsibilities / Ada + colleague\", \"State / Power scheduling\", \"Transition / Teaching diagram\", \"Observation / Bench evidence\", \"Review / Evidence limits\"];\nconst transition = [\"Sleep\", \"→ Measure\", \"Measure\", \"→ Transmit\", \"Transmit\", \"→ Sleep\"];\nexport const faces: FaceDef[] = story.chapters.flatMap(chapter => chapter.beats.flatMap(beat => Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, piece) => ({\n  id: `${beat.id}-${piece}`, beat: beat.id, piece, aspect: beat.id === \"transition.diagram\" ? 2/.42 : 3.65/.46,\n  draw(ctx, width, height, look) {\n    ctx.scale(width / 1000, height / (beat.id === \"transition.diagram\" ? 210 : 126));\n    width = 1000; height = beat.id === \"transition.diagram\" ? 210 : 126;\n    ctx.fillStyle = look.surface.color; ctx.fillRect(0,0,width,height);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = look.faint; ctx.lineWidth = 1;\n    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(width*.13,0); ctx.lineTo(width*.13,height); ctx.moveTo(0,height*.93); ctx.lineTo(width,height*.93); ctx.stroke();\n    ctx.fillStyle = look.accent; ctx.font = `${height*.24}px monospace`; ctx.fillText(String(piece+1).padStart(2,\"0\"),width*.035,height*.58);\n    ctx.fillStyle = look.ink; ctx.font = `${height*.27}px system-ui`; ctx.fillText(beat.id === \"transition.diagram\" ? transition[piece] : table[piece],width*.17,height*.58);\n  },\n}))));\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/formations.ts",
      "sha256": "8ea3a7491fe905c99ba22d4cba78cd81e57a2cbea630a2cbd9b56651f5842ba4",
      "bytes": 1156,
      "text": "import { blankFormation, type BeatFormation, type Formation, type Pose } from \"../lib/story/formation.ts\";\nimport { measure } from \"../lib/story/layouts.ts\";\nimport { story, type BeatId } from \"./story.ts\";\nfunction formation(pieces: Pose[], turn: [number, number] = [-.08, -.16]): Formation {\n  const bounds = measure(pieces);\n  return { ...blankFormation(story.pieces), pieces, span: bounds.span * 1.2, rise: bounds.rise * 1.05, anchor: [.45, .02], turn, near: 5, floor: -4 };\n}\nfunction table(depth: number): Pose[] {\n  return Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => ({ position: [0, (2.5-i)*.53, i*depth], rotation: [0,0,0], size: [3.65,.46] }));\n}\nconst loop: Pose[] = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => {\n  const p = [[-1.15,1.15],[1.15,1.15],[0,-1.05]][Math.floor(i/2)];\n  return { position: [p[0],p[1]-(i%2)*.48,0], rotation: [0,0,0], size: [2,.42] };\n});\nexport const formations = {\n  \"scope.opening\": { rest: formation(table(0)), within: formation(table(.045)) },\n  \"transition.diagram\": { rest: formation(loop, [0,-.08]) },\n  \"review.close\": { rest: formation(table(.045)), within: formation(table(0)) },\n} satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>;\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/content/index.ts",
      "sha256": "a4901be3f3a3eaa8c386da2ed98c35cf0c9a8ec8f9aab33a991a38b9668c53ba",
      "bytes": 427,
      "text": "import type { StoryBundle } from \"@/components/story/types\";\nimport { story } from \"./story\";\nimport { formations } from \"./formations\";\nimport { faces } from \"./faces\";\nimport { looks } from \"./looks\";\nimport { copy } from \"./copy\";\nimport { extras } from \"./extras\";\nimport { links } from \"./links\";\n\nexport const bundle = { story, formations, faces, looks, copy, extras, links, defaultLook: \"light\" } satisfies StoryBundle;\n"
    },

      "text": "import type { Look } from \"../lib/story/looks.ts\";\nexport const looks = [\n  { id: \"light\", name: \"Bench paper\", ground: \"#f2efe6\", ink: \"#282b29\", faint: \"#62635c\", accent: \"#87551c\", surface: { color: \"#fffaf0\", roughness: 1, glows: false }, lights: { ambient: 1.5, key: 2, fill: .5, rim: .6 }, floor: \"none\", shadows: true },\n  { id: \"dark\", name: \"Instrument paper\", ground: \"#202523\", ink: \"#f4f0e5\", faint: \"#bbbeb4\", accent: \"#e5b875\", surface: { color: \"#353c38\", roughness: 1, glows: false }, lights: { ambient: 1.5, key: 2, fill: .5, rim: .6 }, floor: \"none\", shadows: true },\n  { id: \"review\", name: \"Review sheet\", ground: \"#e9edf0\", ink: \"#25313a\", faint: \"#566773\", accent: \"#305d83\", surface: { color: \"#f7f9fa\", roughness: 1, glows: false }, lights: { ambient: 1.5, key: 2, fill: .5, rim: .6 }, floor: \"none\", shadows: true },\n] as const satisfies readonly Look[];\n"

      "text": "import type { ComponentType } from \"react\";\n\n// Each entry is a client component importing its own bundle. Callback-bearing\n// bundles cannot cross a server/client prop boundary.\nexport const sketches: Record<string, ComponentType> = {};\n"

      "bytes": 621,
      "text": "import type { StoryDef, BeatIdOf } from \"../lib/story/story.ts\";\n// Stop 4: the three approved spine beats. The remaining four join after look review.\nexport const story = {\n  pieces: 6,\n  chapters: [\n    { id: \"scope\", number: 1, name: \"Scope\", role: \"opening\", beats: [{ id: \"scope.opening\", height: 1 }] },\n    { id: \"transition\", number: 4, name: \"Transition\", role: \"how\", beats: [{ id: \"transition.diagram\", height: 1.5 }] },\n    { id: \"review\", number: 6, name: \"Review\", role: \"close\", beats: [{ id: \"review.close\", height: 1 }] },\n  ],\n} as const satisfies StoryDef;\nexport type BeatId = BeatIdOf<typeof story>;\n"
    },

      "text": "# Asset provenance and use\n\nAll five public assets below were authored by the evaluation coordinator\nfor this fictional derivative on 11 October 2026. They contain no real\nperson, employer device, third-party photo, logo, font file, firmware,\ncircuit diagram, trace or test report. They are released under the\nrepository's MIT license. Source SVG and HTML files are included, with\nno external URLs, scripts or embedded proprietary resources.\n\nThe coordinator's `source-manifest.json` hashes these exact starting\nfiles. If the build changes or derives an asset, add its source, changes,\nterms and use here; retain the original source. Dimensions below describe\nthe local file, not measurements of a real artifact.\n\n| Public path | Kind and dimensions | Purpose and limits | Alternative text / description |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `/assets/power-states.svg` | Authored SVG, 720 by 620 | Explanatory Sleep, Measure, Transmit loop. These are fictional teaching labels, not actual confirmed firmware states, timing or current readings. Available to link, display and use on faces. | \"Explanatory diagram: Sleep leads to Measure, then Transmit, then back to Sleep. No durations or measured current values are shown.\" Repeat the sequence and its limitation in ordinary HTML. |\n| `/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg` | Authored SVG, 720 by 620 | A firmware command reaches a generic board; the fixture makes a response available to bench instruments. Explanatory relationships only, not a photograph, wiring plan, test result or depiction of the colleague's circuitry. | \"Explanatory bring-up diagram linking firmware command, a generic board, the fixture and a bench observation. It contains no circuit detail.\" Repeat that bring-up checks a new board's basic operation. |\n| `/assets/share-card.svg` | Authored SVG, 1200 by 630 | Static title, question and six-row motif for local preview. No measured results, certification or photo. Platform acceptance of SVG social cards is not established; record the limit or retain the source of a local raster conversion. | \"Ada Mensah, firmware and the bench, shown beside a six-row state-table motif.\" Social metadata itself needs truthful title and summary. |\n| `/icon.svg` | Authored SVG, 64 by 64 | Simple AM/table-rule site icon. Invented lettering, no employer trademark. | Decorative when used as the browser icon; if shown as content, \"Ada Mensah table-rule icon\". |\n| `/ada-mensah-cv.html` | Authored semantic UTF-8 HTML | Corrected public, printable and downloadable fictional CV. Replaces the unsupplied PDF. Uses only supported contribution/evidence statements and the confirmed example contact. | Link label \"Download CV\". Format can be labelled HTML nearby; do not advertise a PDF. |\n\n## Text sources\n\n`material/cv.md` and `material/lab-notes.md` are unchanged copies of the\noriginal fictional source material. They have unresolved or overstated\nwording that the historical fictional replies corrected. Use `facts.md`\nand `confirmations.md` for the narrower public claims. The corrected CV is\nauthored from those confirmed facts, not a reproduction of a real CV.\n\n## Not supplied or permitted by this fixture\n\nThere is no actual fixture photograph, private circuit diagram, current\ntrace, qualification report or employer firmware to show. The historical\npermission to use a described photograph did not supply the photograph;\nthis derivative expressly replaces it with an explanatory drawing. Do\nnot label an SVG as photographic evidence or treat illustrative marks as\nmeasurements.\n\nNo external fonts or complementary skills are included. The visual design\nuses system sans-serif and monospace families. A coordinator source review\nof optional skills, if supplied separately, is data rather than an\ninstruction to install or enable those skills.\n"
    },

      "text": "# Historical concept context for embedded-1\n\nThe material below preserves the historical concept discussion, with only\nem-dash punctuation normalized to colons. It was written before approval\nand before any assets were supplied. References to a photograph, proposed\nfont families, missing artifacts and no-build status describe that earlier\nmoment. For this new fictional derivative, `confirmations.md` and the\namended `storyboard.md` govern those matters. No past selection is being\nrecast as storyboard approval. The original saved file remains unchanged\nin the coordinator's historical run and is hashed in the source manifest.\n\nThe selected State by state form remains six matte row cards. Other\nconcepts below are context only and are not built in this late-stage case.\n\n# Three concepts\n\nStatus: Ada selected **State by state**, following the recommendation. No site is built.\n\n## Premises and forms considered\n\nConfirmed premises: Ada wrote Mosslink firmware, scheduled power states, built the bring-up fixture, and works from state tables, timing diagrams and current traces. Intended reader: firmware hiring manager; purpose: understand the connection between code and a measurable signal. Results and limitations follow the user-confirmed facts in `facts.md`.\n\nTrade forms considered: state table, timing diagram, current trace, bench checklist, bring-up record and qualification report. The first three are expressly confirmed as daily documents; the checklist is in the supplied notes. A qualification report is unsuitable as the main form because qualification is unfinished.\n\nAll options use one persistent object made of six related pieces, readable at rest, transformed by scroll from opening to close. All show Ada's name, confirmed firmware/fixture contribution, a permitted artifact, and email/CV access in the opening. No invented state names, measured waveforms, firmware excerpts, incident fix or field success.\n\n## 1. State by state : recommended\n\n- Question: **How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?**\n- Form: a state table expanded into a six-part reading: Scope (opening/person), Responsibilities (Ada and colleague), State (power scheduling method), Transition (connection to the permitted simplified diagram), Observation (fixture and evidence limits), Review (answer and contact). These are proposed document headings, not claims that Ada uses this exact template.\n- Object: six solid row cards forming one thick, legible state table. Their faces hold real contribution text, excerpts of the permitted simplified diagram, the permitted fixture photo, and evidence annotations. Six is the number of narrative cards, not the number of firmware states.\n- Transformations: Responsibilities separates firmware/scheduling/fixture from the clearly attributed PCB/analogue work; Transition arranges cards into a connected diagram; Observation aligns them as a bench review with the fixture photo and clearly distinguished measurement/projection/status labels.\n- Opening: a flat state table gains depth and unfolds from Ada's confirmed working practice. Name, firmware contribution and permitted fixture preview are readable immediately.\n- Close: the cards reassemble into the table, carrying the answer: Ada's firmware and power-state scheduling can be read alongside the fixture and bench evidence. Email and corrected downloadable CV complete the page.\n- Stands on: confirmed contribution, daily documents, permitted diagram and photo, intended hiring audience, evidence limits.\n- Needs: actual permitted photo and simplified diagram; corrected CV and public email before building. It does not need the incident story, actual private trace or colleague's diagram.\n- Why it is Ada's: the table pairs her specific firmware/scheduling/fixture work with the Mosslink evidence boundaries she has clarified.\n- Visual direction: warm off-white document faces, graphite text, restrained amber connection lines. Labels carry meaning independently of colour. No rendering is produced at this stage.\n\n## 2. Along the timeline\n\n- Question: **How can you read firmware behaviour at the bench?**\n- Form: a timing diagram with six chapters: Scope (opening/person), Signals (Ada's firmware/scheduling/fixture responsibilities), Sequence (power-state scheduling method), Alignment (diagram beside fixture), Measurement (bench evidence and model boundaries), Interpretation (answer/contact). Proposed headings for the site, not an existing project record.\n- Object: six thin, annotated timing strips, stacked into a folded timing sheet at rest. Their faces carry contributions, diagram excerpts, fixture image and evidence notes. These are narrative strips, not asserted signal channels.\n- Transformations: Sequence extends the strips along a common time direction; Alignment layers permitted diagram excerpts beside the fixture photo; Measurement separates measured bench input, projected battery estimate and unfinished qualification into visibly distinct lanes. No invented amplitude, duration or sample values.\n- Opening: the timing sheet unfolds from Ada's named daily document, with her contribution and contact visible.\n- Close: the lanes align and fold back into one sheet; the answer relates code and scheduling to observation through her bench fixture, with email/CV.\n- Stands on: timing diagrams as daily documents, power-state scheduling, fixture ownership, confirmed evidence limits.\n- Needs: permitted diagram/photo and final CV/contact. Timing animations are explanatory and labelled; real trace use would require a separate grant and artifact.\n- Why it is Ada's: her firmware, power scheduling and fixture occupy the same visual timeline, while Mosslink's bench results and projection remain separate.\n- Visual direction: dark graphite bench surface, pale timing strips, amber timing markers; typography remains readable outside the 3D.\n\n## 3. At the bench\n\n- Question: **What can a bench check tell you about new firmware?**\n- Form: a bench checklist with six chapters: Scope (opening/person), Setup (fixture), Ownership (Ada and colleague), Checks (scheduling and simplified diagram), Evidence (sample count, projection and preliminary status), Handover (answer/contact). Proposed headings based on the checklist named in the notes.\n- Object: six rigid checklist leaves clipped into one bench record. Faces carry the fixture photograph, responsibility notes, diagram and evidence statements. The leaves represent the narrative; they are not six sample boards.\n- Transformations: Setup fans the leaves around the fixture image; Ownership separates attributed contribution leaves; Evidence lines the leaves up with explicit statuses: forty assembled, six bench-tested, no customer deployment; projected endurance; preliminary emissions check only. Status markers indicate claims and limits, never fabricated test completion.\n- Opening: the record opens on Ada's own fixture photo, linking the object to something she built.\n- Close: the leaves close into one reviewable record; the answer gives what the bench supports and what remains unproven, followed by email/CV.\n- Stands on: bench checklists in the notes, confirmed fixture work, Ada's definition of bring-up, confirmed sample/qualification/battery limits.\n- Needs: permitted fixture photo and diagram, corrected CV and public email.\n- Why it is Ada's: its central artifact is her bring-up fixture and its checklist explicitly preserves the limits of this engineering-sample project.\n- Visual direction: light grey bench-paper leaves, muted blue annotation, amber pending-status details, with text labels for every status.\n\n## Recommendation and selection\n\nRecommend **State by state**: the state table connects Ada's confirmed power-state scheduling most directly to her desired message about code and measurable signals. Its rows can become both a diagram and a bench evidence review, giving the persistent 3D object a distinct purpose in each chapter.\n\nAda said: “Go with the one you recommend, and give me the whole plan. Still no building.” Selection: **State by state**. Reason: accepted the recommendation connecting her power-state scheduling to measurable bench evidence. The full storyboard is in `storyboard.md`; awaiting approval of that script. No construction follows automatically.\n"

      "text": "# Fictional confirmations for this build\n\nCreated by the evaluation coordinator on 11 October 2026. Ada Mensah,\nReedglass Sensing and Mosslink are invented. These statements are new\nfictional user input for `embedded-1`, not quotations from the historical\nplanning conversation or the real repository author.\n\nThe historical conversation ended with an unapproved storyboard and no\npermission to build. For this derivative only, the fictional person has\napproved the amended `storyboard.md` and requests the build through spine,\nchapters and finish. The external run protocol controls when each next\nstop is authorized; do not collapse all approval gates into the first turn.\n\n## Scope and artifact decisions\n\n- The site is for a firmware hiring manager. It should show how I connect\n  code to a measurable signal, with email and a downloadable CV available\n  near the beginning and the end.\n- Use `ada@example.com` as the fictional public contact. The example-domain\n  mailbox is a deliberate fixture value. Link to it; do not send mail,\n  claim delivery was tested, or replace it with a made-up live address.\n- Keep State by state, its six narrative row cards, six chapters and seven\n  beats. The cards are not six firmware states or six sample boards.\n- A real fixture photograph is still unavailable. Replace the photo in\n  this derivative with `/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg`. It is an explanatory\n  drawing, not evidence of the appearance of a real board or fixture.\n- Use `/assets/power-states.svg` as an explanatory three-state teaching\n  diagram. Sleep, Measure and Transmit and their loop are authored for this\n  fixture. Do not claim they reproduce actual Mosslink firmware, a current\n  trace, durations, current values, or the unresolved radio-awake incident.\n- All supplied SVGs were authored for this fixture and may be displayed,\n  linked, resized and used as face textures under the MIT license. Do not\n  invent a photo, circuitry, waveform, test report or private firmware.\n- The corrected CV is `/ada-mensah-cv.html`, a semantic, printable HTML\n  document with readable text. An ordinary link with a download attribute\n  is sufficient. The historical PDF requirement is explicitly replaced.\n- Use local system sans-serif and monospace fonts. No external font or\n  image download is needed. Offer the three approved looks at the spine\n  review; the fixed next-turn choice is defined by the run protocol.\n- At 767 CSS pixels wide or narrower, use static single-column HTML and\n  the supplied illustrations. Do not mount a scene or require its WebGL\n  code for this mode. Reduced motion also uses the static presentation at\n  every width. Normal desktop mode keeps the scroll-driven six-piece scene.\n- This scope has one complete Mosslink case on the main page and no\n  separate project route. It has no testimonials, blog, chat or translation.\n- No employer role or dates are newly confirmed. Leave them out of the\n  site and corrected CV rather than inventing a current employment claim.\n- Legal details and hosting jurisdiction remain a prepublication decision.\n  This local experiment does not publish, submit forms, send messages or\n  claim legal compliance.\n\n## Core wording to keep in readable HTML\n\nThe following sentences are approved for this fictional derivative. Keep\nthem verbatim in the relevant beat's visible HTML so the coordinator can\ncheck the factual contract independently. Draft headings, transitions and\nsurrounding prose at stop 5 without adding unsupported claims. The fixed\nheadings in the storyboard identify beats and are also part of this case.\n\n1. Firmware is code that controls a physical device.\n2. Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation.\n3. I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture.\n4. A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end.\n5. Forty engineering samples were assembled. Six were tested on the bench. None went to customers.\n6. Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle.\n7. The longest run was 72 hours.\n8. One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.\n9. Explanatory schematic, not a measured trace or a firmware specification.\n10. Explanatory schematic, not a photograph or a circuit diagram.\n11. I connect firmware decisions to bench observations through power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture, while keeping the evidence limits visible.\n\nNo part of this new scope says I fixed the radio-awake issue, designed the\nPCB, deployed a customer pilot, measured two years of battery endurance,\ncompleted qualification, or have another project or testimonial to add.\n"

      "text": "# Scope decisions\n\nThese decisions are coordinator-authored fictional confirmations for the\namended build. They do not retroactively change the historical run. The\nperson's new confirmation is in `confirmations.md`; source limitations\nremain in `facts.md`.\n\n| Site checklist item | Disposition | Who decided and why |\n|---|---|---|\n| Way around the page | Build: six chapter anchors, skip-to-content and skip-to-contact | Historical planner; derivative confirms short visits and keyboard access. |\n| A project's own page | Never in this fixture: one complete Mosslink case on the main page | Historical planner; fictional derivative approves this explicit exception. It does not test general project-page support. |\n| Every project listed | Build: Mosslink, the only supplied project | Source scope and fictional confirmation; no invented project grid. |\n| Contact and CV | Build: `mailto:ada@example.com` and corrected downloadable HTML CV at opening and close | Fictional confirmation resolves address and format; mailbox delivery is not tested. |\n| What others say | Never in this fixture | Historical person supplied no testimonials; do not invent them. |\n| Languages | Build: English only; later if translations are supplied | Historical planner and derivative source language. |\n| Shared-link preview and icon | Build: truthful title/summary, supplied static share-card SVG and icon; record platform format limits | Derivative coordinator authored local assets; social-platform compatibility is not claimed without a validated raster derivative and platform check. |\n| Missing address | Build: readable 404 with Home and Email Ada links | Historical planner; useful even for a one-page scope. |\n| Blog | Never in this fixture | No writing or request supplied. |\n| Chat | Never in this fixture | Person requested email and CV, no chat. |\n| Legal notice where required | Later, before any publication | Hosting jurisdiction and legal particulars are absent. Local evaluation authorizes no publishing or legal-compliance claim. |\n\n## Other explicit choices\n\n- Keep the selected six-row State by state form, six chapters and seven\n  beats. Eight desktop viewports are a budget, not a reason for blank\n  mobile screens. This is a card regression, not a new object-family proof.\n- Replace the missing fixture photo with an honestly labelled explanatory\n  schematic. Use the supplied teaching diagram without claiming real\n  firmware topology or measured timing. No private circuitry or trace.\n- Use system sans-serif and monospace fonts because no licensed named\n  font files are supplied. Keep all three appearances available for the\n  spine's actual choice and subsequent review.\n- Use static HTML and drawings on narrow screens, under reduced motion,\n  without JavaScript or without working WebGL. Normal desktop still uses\n  a six-piece scroll scene.\n- Include no unconfirmed employment chronology, incident resolution,\n  influence story, certification, field results or extra projects.\n- Keep source and permission records, test results and handover notes in\n  the local project. Publishing and external messages remain outside scope.\n\n## Stop 4 implementation decisions — 11 October 2026\n\n- The current working page contains only Scope, Transition and Review, as\n  requested for the spine review. Their IDs and chapter numbers match the\n  approved full storyboard. Four remaining beats, their copy and the six\n  chapter navigation are reserved for stop 5 after the look choice.\n- All three appearances use the identical six rows and formations. Query\n  values are `light` (Bench paper, default), `dark` (Instrument paper), and\n  `review` (Review sheet). Change palettes in `content/looks.ts`.\n- Use an ordinary local SVG preview and expansion link alongside the opening\n  and transition text. A compact desktop preview expands to a large static\n  illustration when the scene is off. This keeps its explanatory limit next\n  to the image. The\n  browser matrix declares this fixture's static choices explicitly rather\n  than retaining the engine's scene-on expectation for those cases.\n- Keep the look switch available while scrolling. The engine keeps its\n  original default for other bundles; new ratios are bounded by validation.\n- Static header navigation is positioned against the story root, outside\n  the content's top spacing. The checker now accepts optional `--jobs=3`\n  to run independent cases in batches on the same production server; its\n  default is still sequential. Full scope and all failure checks remain.\n  `--wait=1000` is the final screenshot settle interval. No selected-case or\n  skip-build run is presented as a full acceptance run.\n"

      "text": "# Confirmed facts and their sources\n\nThis is a fictional derivative. `confirmations.md` distinguishes its new\ndecisions from the historical source. The old CV is preserved in\n`material/cv.md` as conflicting source material, not publication-ready copy.\n\n| Fact | Source and limits |\n|---|---|\n| Ada Mensah works with embedded firmware for physical devices | Original `material/cv.md`; confirmed audience and contribution in the saved fictional replies. No current employer/title/date claim is needed. |\n| Mosslink is an environmental sensor | Original `material/cv.md`. It is an invented project, not a real product or employer disclosure. |\n| Ada wrote firmware, scheduled power states and built the bring-up fixture | Historical fictional confirmation overrides \"Owned the low-power sensor design\" in the original CV. |\n| A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end | Historical fictional confirmation. Ada must not be credited with this circuitry. |\n| Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle | Historical fictional confirmation plus `material/lab-notes.md`. No exact reporting interval, current value, capacity, climate condition or model ownership is supplied. |\n| The longest run was 72 hours | Historical fictional confirmation plus `material/lab-notes.md`. It does not establish projected endurance, field endurance or weather testing. |\n| Forty engineering samples assembled; six tested on the bench; none sent to customers | Historical fictional confirmation overrides \"forty-unit pilot\". No field pilot, product launch or forty-unit verification. |\n| One preliminary emissions check passed; full qualification unfinished | Historical fictional confirmation overrides \"Qualification: emissions pass\". No certification claim. |\n| State tables, timing diagrams and current traces are daily working documents | Historical fictional confirmation plus lab notes. No actual trace is supplied or licensed for display. |\n| Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation | Historical fictional confirmation. |\n| The audience is a firmware hiring manager; email and downloadable CV are enough | Historical fictional confirmation. |\n| No old site and no testimonials | Historical fictional confirmation. |\n| Public email, schematic assets, HTML CV and static-mode choices are confirmed for this derivative | New, explicitly fictional `confirmations.md`. |\n\n## Resolved source disagreements\n\nUse the corrected contribution, projection, sample and preliminary-status\nwording above. The original CV remains unchanged in `material/` for source\nprovenance. The public corrected CV contains only the narrower claims.\n\n## Omitted because evidence is absent\n\nThe lab notes mention a failed transmission leaving the radio awake. They\ndo not establish who diagnosed or fixed it, a measured outcome, or a public\nincident account. Do not turn it into a success story. No real trace,\ncircuit diagram, employer firmware, qualification report, photograph or\nfield deployment is supplied. The new explanatory SVGs are not substitutes\nfor those records and must retain their visible explanatory labels.\n\nNo influence story, testimonial, additional project, career chronology or\nconfirmed current employer title/date is supplied. The scope avoids them.\n\n## Provenance of the confirmations\n\nThe historical source is the fictional `embedded` person and the saved\n`codex-opening-1/embedded/with-2` conversation. The coordinator retains the\noriginal files and hashes outside this actor workspace. All new scope\ndecisions are enumerated in `confirmations.md`; none is attributed to the\nreal repository author. Original facts do not become real-world claims by\nappearing in this build fixture.\n"

      "text": "# Stop 4: local spine for appearance review\n\n## Person's words and current gate\n\nOn 11 October 2026 the user said yes to the derivative `storyboard.md` and\nfictional `confirmations.md`, explicitly authorized building beyond the\nStoryfolio skill's planning-only ending, and asked: “First build the spine:\nthe opening, a representative middle chapter and the ending, in two or\nthree looks for the same approved object. Let me scroll the working result\nand choose a look before completing the rest.” Everything stays local.\n\nNo concept selection was restarted. The selected State by state object is\nsix matte narrative row cards. These are neither six firmware states nor\nsix physical boards. The skill was read; the user's explicit continuation\nsupersedes its planning-only ending. No look choice or later copy approval\nhas been fabricated.\n\n## Implemented\n\nThe plain starter has been replaced with three stable spine beats:\n`scope.opening`, `transition.diagram`, `review.close`. Original chapter\nnumbers 1, 4 and 6 remain visible. Six persistent rows gain shallow depth,\nseparate into three labelled teaching-loop pairs, then reassemble. All\nthree looks use the same geometry, words and scroll progression.\n\nBench paper is the default (`?look=light` or no query). Instrument paper\nuses `?look=dark`; Review sheet uses `?look=review`. The switch preserves\nscroll, fragment and other query parameters. The palette lives in\n`content/looks.ts`; formations and face drawings live beside it.\n\nServer-rendered English text contains the approved opening definition,\nAda's contribution, diagram limits and closing answer with projection,\n72-hour run and unfinished qualification limits. The two local explanatory\nSVGs are shown and linked, with their recorded alternative text. Email and\ndownloadable corrected HTML CV are available in the header, opening and\nclose. A local missing-page view has Home and Email Ada links.\n\nStatic modes use readable single-column text and large diagrams. At\n767 CSS pixels or less, and with reduced motion at every width, the dynamic\nscene never mounts. No JavaScript, no WebGL or renderer failure keeps the\nspine text, diagrams and links. The current spine has three beats; the\ncomplete seven-beat static contract becomes applicable when stop 5 is built.\n\nEngine changes are limited to the static-mode gate, optional bounded face\naspect ratios for legible wide row textures, and explicit check-matrix\nstatic-mode declarations. Optional starter extras and piece-overlay links\nare not used by this spine. Existing engine defaults remain for other\nbundles. System sans-serif and monospace fonts require no external service.\n\n## Environment and validation\n\nActual inspection found a supplied Next.js 16.3.8 starter and locked\npackages, not a prior user portfolio. Node is v22.22.1. `npm ci` hit a\nblocked registry request; `npm ci --offline` successfully installed all\n392 locked packages from the available cache. This is not a fresh advisory\nreview. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/storyfolio-browser-cache npm run\nbrowsers` passed. Browser runtime libraries were supplied locally via\n`LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/storyfolio-browser-libs/root/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`.\n\nRead the installed Next.js 16 documentation for dynamic client loading,\nmetadata, missing routes and Link. The share SVG remains a local source\nasset: social-platform acceptance of SVG previews has not been tested.\nMetadata currently resolves against localhost; an actual publication URL\nand legal details are prepublication work.\n\n`npm test`: 131 tests passed. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint`: passed.\nThe final fresh production browser run is under\n`checks/2026-10-11T01-55-22-591Z/`; all 18 browser cases passed after a fresh build using `--jobs=3 --wait=1000`.\nVisual review is recorded in `review.md`, and compact results are committed\nin `check-results.json`. Earlier interrupted runs are diagnostic only.\nScreenshot review corrected stretched/blurred row lettering, static\nheader overlap and the shorter-desktop appearance-switch position.\n\n`scripts/check-spine.mjs` additionally checks actual scene chunk requests,\nstatic phone/reduced modes, desktop deep-link and chapter-navigation state,\nkeyboard reachability, email/CV attributes, all supplied assets and the\nmissing-route response and links. It writes its results and extra screenshots\nunder the final run's `supplemental/` folder.\n\n## Local use and repository history\n\nRun `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npm run dev` from this project and open the\nprinted local address. Scroll each appearance before choosing one. No site\nhas been published and no email has been sent.\n\nThis sandbox exposes an empty read-only `.git` placeholder, so ordinary\ngit cannot create repository history there. Local history is stored in\n`.storyfolio-git/` inside this project instead. Use\n`git --git-dir=.storyfolio-git --work-tree=. status` (and the same prefix for\nlog/diff/commit). It is ignored as a working-tree path. Only known project\nsources and story records are included; injected credential placeholders,\ndependencies, builds and screenshots are excluded.\n\n## Next\n\nWait for the person's scroll-based choice among Bench paper, Instrument\npaper and Review sheet. Then implement Responsibilities, State and both\nObservation beats from the approved storyboard, preserving all seven IDs,\nsix chapter anchors and eleven exact confirmed sentences. Offer opening\nand closing surrounding-copy choices at stop 5. Do not infer those choices\nfrom approval of the storyboard or facts. Finish checks only after that\nreview. Automated Chromium checks and fictional confirmations are not\nreal-phone performance evidence or a real repository author's review.\n"

      "text": "# Spine review — ready for the person's look choice\n\n11 October 2026. This is stop 4, not approval of the completed site.\n\nThe local working spine contains Ada Mensah, Reading transitions and Code\nbeside evidence, carried by the same six row cards in all three looks.\nUse the appearance switch to compare Bench paper, Instrument paper and\nReview sheet while scrolling. No choice has yet been received.\n\n## Checks performed\n\n| Command / inspection | Result |\n|---|---|\n| `npm ci` | Registry request blocked; installation recovered with `npm ci --offline` (392 locked packages) |\n| `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/storyfolio-browser-cache npm run browsers` | Passed |\n| `npm test` | 131 passed, 0 failed |\n| `npm run typecheck` | Passed |\n| `npm run lint` | Passed |\n| `npm run check -- --jobs=3 --wait=1000` with supplied browser cache and libraries | Fresh production build; full matrix, 18/18 passed |\n| `node scripts/check-spine.mjs checks/2026-10-11T01-55-22-591Z/supplemental` with the same browser environment | Static chunk loading, desktop navigation/deep link, keyboard reachability, supplied assets, email/CV attributes and missing-page checks passed |\n| Visual inspection | All 93 matrix screenshots opened through labelled contact sheets; representative original desktop and phone images also opened. Previous runs were stopped for\nvisual corrections or terminated before completion; they are not acceptance\nruns. The final checker still defaults to sequential execution; optional\nbatching preserved the entire matrix within the environment's runtime limit.\n\n## Observations\n\nThe desktop table stays framed beside the prose, separates into Sleep,\nMeasure and Transmit teaching pairs, then returns to its row formation.\nThe third appearance changes the palette to cool paper and blue annotations;\nit keeps the same object and factual labels. All looks keep readable text\nand labelled explanatory drawings. The short-desktop switch is above the\nrows. Phone header, chapter links, switch and opening now have separate\nspace. Large static diagrams are readable without the canvas.\n\nPhone and reduced-motion contexts each mounted zero canvases and requested\nzero identified scene chunks. These were corrected\nbefore the final complete run. Static snapshots can start partway through a\nsection because the engine samples scroll rests; the full text remains in\nordinary document flow and is reachable by scrolling.\n\n## Scope and limits\n\nThe remaining four beats and their core sentences are intentionally deferred\nuntil the person chooses a look. The full seven-beat content contract has\nnot yet been completed or approved. No fictional response is counted as\nreal scrolling review. No real phone performance, mail delivery, legal\nadequacy, deployment or external social-card compatibility is established.\nThe corrected CV is HTML. The two diagrams are explanatory SVGs, not\nphotographs, circuitry, measured traces or specifications.\n\n## Awaiting\n\nThe person's choice: Bench paper, Instrument paper or Review sheet. After\nthat, continue stop 5 without restarting the concept: add Responsibilities,\nState and both Observation beats, keep all eleven confirmed sentences and\nsix chapter links, and offer the requested surrounding-copy choices.\n"

      "text": "# State by state: amended build storyboard\n\nApproved fictional derivative for `embedded-1`, 11 October 2026. The\nhistorical storyboard remains unchanged in the saved evaluation. This\nversion replaces missing assets explicitly as `confirmations.md` describes.\nThe run's external continuation contract permits the current build stop;\nlater review replies authorize later stops. No deployment is requested.\n\n## Governing idea\n\n**How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?** A state table\nbecomes a responsibility table, an explanatory diagram and an evidence\nledger, then returns to a complete table. Six persistent matte row cards\ncarry the story. They are narrative pieces, not six firmware states or six\nphysical boards. This is a card-engine fixture, not a non-sheet proof.\n\nThe audience is a firmware hiring manager. State Ada's contribution and\nits limits clearly in HTML. The scene supplements that text. The colleague's\nPCB/analogue contribution stays distinct from Ada's firmware, scheduling\nand fixture work; measured inputs, projected endurance and unfinished\nqualification stay distinct from one another.\n\n## Chapters and beats\n\nUse these stable chapter and beat IDs. Each chapter contains a corresponding\nsemantic section and heading. Each beat uses the engine's `data-beat`\nattribute. The heading for `scope.opening` is the page's single h1.\n\n| Chapter ID and label | Beat ID and heading | Desktop screens | Formation and HTML content |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `scope`, Scope | `scope.opening`, Ada Mensah | 1 | Six flat rows gain shallow depth. Name, question, firmware meaning, contribution and the explicitly explanatory fixture preview. Contact and CV available immediately. |\n| `responsibilities`, Responsibilities | `responsibilities.split`, Who made what | 1 | Same rows separate into clearly attributed groups. Exact Ada and colleague contribution sentences from confirmations 3 and 4. |\n| `state`, State | `state.table`, Scheduling power states | 1 | Rows align as a ruled table. Explain state tables as a daily working document and scheduling as part of Ada's confirmed contribution. Do not claim actual state-machine entries. |\n| `transition`, Transition | `transition.diagram`, Reading transitions | 1.5 | Rows form the supplied explanatory Sleep, Measure, Transmit loop. Keep its teaching-diagram limit visible using sentence 9. No timing/current values, invented branches or incident fix. Link to the SVG at readable size. |\n| `observation`, Observation | `observation.fixture`, Checking basic operation | 1 | Shallow bench review with the fixture schematic prominent. Use bring-up definition, sentence 2, and explanatory limit, sentence 10. Link to the SVG at readable size. |\n| `observation`, Observation | `observation.evidence`, What the bench supports | 1.5 | Evidence ledger. Sentences 5, 6, 7 and 8 preserve assembled/tested/customer status, projection, longest run and unfinished qualification. Never imply the 72-hour run validated two years. |\n| `review`, Review | `review.close`, Code beside evidence | 1 | Rows reassemble into the opening table. Use closing answer, sentence 11, alongside the evidence limits; repeat email and downloadable corrected CV. |\n\nApproximate desktop budget: eight viewport lengths. Static mobile height\nfollows readable content; do not retain eight empty desktop scroll screens.\nContent must stay available after arriving at every beat, including both\nbeats in Observation. Every exact core sentence must be in visible HTML,\nnot only a card texture, aria label or hidden fallback.\n\n## Spine review at stop 4\n\nBuild the opening, Transition from the middle, and Review first. Offer\nBench paper, Instrument paper and Review sheet as three appearances of\nthe same object and story. The person picks a look by scrolling. The rest\nof the body need not be complete until stop 5. Do not fabricate approval.\n\n## Look and motion\n\n| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Card surface |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Bench paper | Warm off-white | Graphite | Muted amber | Matte cream, fine ruled lines |\n| Instrument paper | Deep graphite | Pale ivory | Muted amber | Dark matte, fine pale rules |\n| Review sheet | Cool light grey | Charcoal | Restrained blue | Light grey, restrained annotations |\n\nBench paper starts as the default. System sans-serif prose and monospace\nnotation replace the two unsupplied named font families in the historical\nplan. All looks must preserve contrast, meaning and readable evidence\nlabels. No glossy circuitry, sci-fi display or measured-looking waveform.\n\nNormal desktop scroll drives short translations and rotations of the same\nsix cards. Stable rests, no forced horizontal movement, autoplay or\nscroll hijacking. Keep the camera steady except modest diagram framing.\nChapter links jump to the correct content; settled scene state must agree\nwith deep links. Complete text never depends on a face being visible.\n\n## Static modes and accessibility\n\nAt widths of 767 CSS pixels or less, use a single-column static page with\nchapter anchors and large readable supplied diagrams. Do not mount or\ndownload a scene-only/WebGL chunk to read this mode. At wider widths with\nreduced-motion preference, use the same static content with no scene\ncanvas or scroll-driven movement. These are explicit fixture choices that\noverride the engine's default mobile and reduced-motion animation behavior.\n\nNo JavaScript, unavailable WebGL and a renderer failure all retain the\ncomplete seven-beat HTML, diagrams, navigation, email and CV. A CSS-hidden\nor invisible animated canvas is not the chosen static mode. A desktop\nwithout those constraints must have the intended scene.\n\nThere is one h1 and unique IDs for both Observation beats. Meaning is not\nencoded by color alone. Images have the alternative text recorded in\n`assets.md`, diagram descriptions are ordinary HTML, links work with the\nkeyboard and focus remains visible. A simple link to each SVG is the\napproved keyboard-operable expansion; no dialog or complex zoom is needed.\n\n## Navigation and required link labels\n\nA compact header offers `Email Ada` (`mailto:ada@example.com`), `Download\nCV` (`/ada-mensah-cv.html`, with download behavior), and `Skip to contact`\n(`#review`). Repeat email and CV in Review. Keep all six chapter anchors\nreachable, as well as skip-to-content. At the relevant beats use `View\npower-state schematic` (`/assets/power-states.svg`) and `View fixture\nschematic` (`/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg`).\n\nThe page metadata identifies Ada Mensah and firmware work. English is the\ndocument language. The supplied share SVG and icon are illustrative local\nassets; using them does not prove social platforms accept SVG previews.\nState that support limit in the final handover instead of asserting a\ntested cross-platform card. If the build converts the share card to a\nsupported raster format locally, record that derivative and keep its source.\n\n## Copy, scope and finish\n\nAt stop 5 draft the surrounding prose from `facts.md` and show choices for\nthe key opening and closing wording. Retain the eleven confirmed sentences\nand seven fixed headings. They are part of the fixture's acceptance\ncontract, not measurements or externally validated project claims.\n\nEvery site-checklist decision is recorded in `decided-for-you.md`.\nMosslink's one complete case stays on the main page. A missing-address page\nhas a Home link and email; legal details remain a prepublication task.\n\nAt stop 6 check all three looks, normal desktop, static phone, reduced\nmotion, JavaScript/WebGL failures, keyboard navigation, deep links,\ncontact/CV links, all assets, and missing-route behavior. Record commands,\nresults and limitations in the project. A scripted fictional approval\ncannot stand in for the real repository author's scrolling review.\n"

      "text": "import { defineConfig, globalIgnores } from \"eslint/config\";\nimport nextVitals from \"eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals\";\nimport nextTs from \"eslint-config-next/typescript\";\nexport default defineConfig([\n  ...nextVitals,\n  ...nextTs,\n  globalIgnores([\".next/**\", \"out/**\", \"checks/**\", \"next-env.d.ts\"]),\n]);\n"
