    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/scripts/check-lib.mjs",
      "sha256": "e32668b8d452c4153b16fd5bd36ae11f2112f66bf0383ed8b88f755ed0d83c07",
      "bytes": 4710,
      "text": "import { TRAVEL } from \"../lib/story/timeline.ts\";\n\n/** Empty ignore values mean no exception. A nonempty value is an explicit regex. */\nexport function optionalPattern(value) {\n  return value ? new RegExp(String(value)) : null;\n}\n\nexport function expectedRequestReason({ url, resourceType, failure }, { ignore = null, block = null, noJavaScript = false, pageUrl } = {}) {\n  if (block?.test(url)) return \"intentionally blocked request\";\n  if (ignore?.test(url)) return \"explicit ignore pattern\";\n  if (noJavaScript && resourceType === \"script\" && [\"csp\", \"net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CSP\"].includes(failure)) {\n    try {\n      const request = new URL(url);\n      if (request.origin === new URL(pageUrl).origin && /^\\/_next\\/static\\/.+\\.js$/.test(request.pathname)) {\n        return \"JavaScript-disabled CSP rejection of a same-origin Next.js script preload\";\n      }\n    } catch { /* Invalid URLs cannot qualify for this narrow exception. */ }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport function requestProblem({ url, status, failure, resourceType }, options = {}) {\n  if (expectedRequestReason({ url, resourceType, failure }, options)) return null;\n  if (failure) return `request failed (${failure}): ${url}`;\n  return status >= 400 ? `HTTP ${status}: ${url}` : null;\n}\n\nexport function storyContract(story, looks) {\n  const ids = story.chapters.flatMap(chapter => chapter.beats.map(beat => beat.id));\n  if (!ids.length || new Set(ids).size !== ids.length || ids.some(id => !/^[\\w.-]+$/.test(id))) {\n    throw new Error(\"The check contract needs unique, nonempty beat IDs\");\n  }\n  const lookIds = looks.map(look => look.id);\n  if (!lookIds.length || new Set(lookIds).size !== lookIds.length) throw new Error(\"The check contract needs unique look IDs\");\n  return { ids, lookIds };\n}\n\n/** The contract comes from content, never from whatever the first browser happened to render. */\nexport function checkMatrix({ ids, lookIds }, probes = {}) {\n  const common = [`--expect-beats=${ids.length}`, `--expect-ids=${ids.join(\",\")}`, \"--beats\", \"--inside=.story-control\"];\n  const matrix = [];\n  for (const look of lookIds) {\n    const expected = [...common, `--expect-look=${look}`];\n    matrix.push(\n      { name: `${look}-wide`, look, flags: [...expected, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--expect-scene=on\", \"--positions=start,mid,end\", \"--late-shaders=40000\"] },\n      { name: `${look}-short`, look, flags: [...expected, \"--size=1280x720\", \"--expect-scene=on\", \"--late-shaders=40000\"] },\n      { name: `${look}-phone`, look, flags: [...expected, \"--size=390x844\", \"--touch\", probes.staticPhone ? \"--expect-scene=off\" : \"--expect-scene=on\", ...(probes.staticPhone ? [\"--hidden=canvas\"] : [])] },\n      { name: `${look}-reduced`, look, flags: [...expected, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--reduced-motion\", probes.staticReduced ? \"--expect-scene=off\" : \"--expect-scene=on\", \"--positions=start,mid,end\", ...(probes.staticReduced ? [\"--hidden=canvas\"] : [\"--assert-still=300\"])] },\n      { name: `${look}-no-webgl`, look, flags: [...expected, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--no-webgl\", \"--expect-scene=off\"] },\n    );\n  }\n  matrix.push(\n    { name: \"no-js\", look: lookIds[0], flags: [...common, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--no-js\", \"--expect-selector=h1\", \"--hidden=canvas,.story-look-switch,.story-control\"] },\n    { name: \"context-loss\", look: lookIds[0], flags: [...common, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--lose-context\", \"--expect-scene=off\"] },\n  );\n  if (lookIds.length > 1) matrix.push({ name: \"look-switch\", look: lookIds[0], flags: [...common, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--expect-scene=on\", `--look-cycle=${lookIds.slice(0, 2).join(\",\")}`, `--expect-look=${lookIds[0]}`] });\n  if (probes.overlay) {\n    if (!ids.includes(probes.overlay.beat) || !probes.overlay.selector) throw new Error(\"The overlay probe needs a declared beat and selector\");\n    matrix.push({ name: \"keyboard-overlay\", look: lookIds[0], flags: [...common, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--expect-scene=on\", `--keyboard=${probes.overlay.selector}`, `--keyboard-at=${probes.overlay.beat}`] });\n  }\n  if (probes.lazyExtra) matrix.push({ name: \"failed-extra\", look: lookIds[0], flags: [...common, \"--size=1440x900\", \"--expect-scene=on\", \"--block-late-chunks\"] });\n  return matrix;\n}\n/** Match playhead's rest intervals, including arrival before later blocks reach the top. */\nexport function beatRestSamples(boxes, viewport, positions = [\"end\"]) {\n  let arrived = 0;\n  const travel = Math.max(1, TRAVEL * viewport);\n  return boxes.map(box => {\n    const leaves = Math.max(arrived, box.top + box.height - viewport);\n    const samples = positions.map(position => ({\n      position,\n      top: arrived + (leaves - arrived) * ({ start: 0, mid: 0.5, end: 1 }[position]),\n    }));\n    arrived = leaves + travel;\n    return samples;\n  });\n}\n\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "inputs/fixture/scripts/check-lib.test.mjs",
      "sha256": "c22b87f0a7461a84ad20fb33c47022615223cc1f7e7542e28004c2d48c452e10",
      "bytes": 4805,
      "text": "import assert from \"node:assert/strict\";\nimport test from \"node:test\";\nimport { beatRestSamples, checkMatrix, expectedRequestReason, optionalPattern, requestProblem, storyContract } from \"./check-lib.mjs\";\nimport { playhead } from \"../lib/story/timeline.ts\";\n\ntest(\"later tall beats sample their whole dwell from arrival, not just their block top\", () => {\n  const boxes = [{ top: 0, height: 2000 }, { top: 2000, height: 2000 }, { top: 4000, height: 1000 }];\n  const samples = beatRestSamples(boxes, 1000, [\"start\", \"mid\", \"end\"]);\n  assert.deepEqual(samples[1].map(sample => sample.top), [1400, 2200, 3000]);\n  for (let i = 0; i < samples.length; i++) {\n    for (const [position, sample] of samples[i].entries()) {\n      const head = playhead(sample.top, 1000, boxes);\n      assert.equal(head.beat, i);\n      assert.equal(head.dwell, position / 2);\n    }\n  }\n});\n\ntest(\"empty request ignore does not suppress HTTP errors or failures without responses\", () => {\n  const ignore = optionalPattern(\"\");\n  assert.equal(ignore, null);\n  assert.match(requestProblem({ url: \"http://localhost/chunk.js\", status: 404 }, { ignore }), /HTTP 404/);\n  assert.match(requestProblem({ url: \"http://localhost/chunk.js\", failure: \"net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED\" }, { ignore }), /ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED/);\n PLAYWRIGHT_CORE optionally overrides the\n  engine's own playwright-core install:\n\n    PLAYWRIGHT_CORE=/home/me/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/playwright-core \\\n      node scripts/shoot.mjs --url=http://localhost:3000/ --out=/tmp/home --beats\n\n  Options\n    --url=URL              page to open (required)\n    --out=DIR              where the screenshots go (required)\n    --size=WxH             viewport, default 1440x900\n    --scale=N              device pixel ratio, default 1\n    --beats                one screenshot per [data-beat] block, taken at the\n                           end of that beat's rest\n    --reduced-motion       emulate prefers-reduced-motion\n    --touch                emulate a touch device, whose pointer is coarse:\n                           the scene then takes its lighter path\n    --no-webgl             start Chromium with 3D disabled\n    --no-js                load the page with JavaScript switched off\n    --ignore=REGEX         failed requests to overlook; they are left out of the failed-\n                           request check\n    --inside=CSS           with --beats: fail if anything matching the selector\n                           is showing but runs off the side of the screen\n    --scroll=PX            without --beats: scroll this far down before the\n                           click and the screenshot\n    --wait=MS              how long to let the page settle after each scroll,\n                           default 2200. --click=CSS            without --beats: click the first match, then fail\n                           if what was being read has moved on the screen,\n                           which is how switching       "text": "I’ll use the Storyfolio skill to continue the saved spine in Bench paper. I’ll read the handover and engine contract, implement the remaining beats, and pause for your copy choice before the finishing pass.\n\n\nThe saved contract has six chapters, seven beats and eleven fixed factual sentences. I’ll keep those intact, add the four remaining beats to the existing six-row scene, and use clearly labelled teaching content without inventing firmware entries or measurements. The copy choices will cover surrounding prose only.\n\n\nAll seven beats are now implemented. Responsibilities separates Ada’s work from the colleague’s circuitry; State labels the rows as narrative content; Observation separates the fixture explanation from the evidence ledger. I’ll check the production draft and screenshots before presenting the opening and closing copy options.\n\n\nThe first screenshots show the new beats and evidence limits clearly. They also caught the longer opening touching the navigation on a short desktop screen. I’ve removed a repeated project label to give it more room; I’ll verify that fix while keeping your copy choice open.\n\n\nThe unit tests, type check and lint pass. So far, the production browser checks have passed for Bench paper and Instrument paper, including static phone, reduced-motion and unavailable-WebGL modes. The draft uses my recommended opening and closing provisionally; both choices will remain yours before the finishing pass.\n\n\nThe fresh short-desktop screenshot confirms the opening no longer overlaps the navigation. The supplemental checks also pass: all seven beats and eleven fixed sentences are present, chapter links settle correctly, and static phone and reduced-motion modes fetch no scene chunk. I’m finishing the draft’s visual review before pausing for copy.\n\n\nThe local draft is available at [http://127.0.0.1:3000](http://127.0.0.1:3000), with Bench paper selected. The new formations keep contribution and evidence labels beside the prose. I’m recording the check results and handover, then I’ll pause for your opening and closing copy choice.\n\n\nThe remaining beats are implemented in **Bench paper**, completing the seven-beat draft. [Open the local preview](http://127.0.0.1:3000).\n\nAll eleven fixed sentences remain intact. Tests, typecheck, lint and all 18 production browser cases pass; screenshots were inspected. Decisions, copy options and handover are saved and committed locally.\n\n| Placement | Recommended | Alternative |\n|---|---|---|\n| Opening | **O1:** “On Mosslink, an environmental sensor, my work spans firmware, power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture.” | **O2:** “Mosslink is an environmental sensor. My contribution was firmware, power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture.” |\n| Closing | **C1:** “Read the firmware contribution alongside the bench evidence and its limits.” | **C2:** “For the contribution and evidence together, download my CV or email me.” |\n\nI recommend **O1 + C1** for their clear scope and emphasis on evidence.\n\nChoose **O1/O2 and C1/C2**, or send edits. I’m stopping here for your copy choice before the finishing pass.\n\nChecks used local Chromium; no physical-phone test or real-person review is claimed.\n"

-lc 'cat /tmp/storyfolio-evals/build-embedded-completion-1-HA9i68/.agents/skills/storyfolio/SKILL.md'\",\"aggregated_output\":\"---\\nname: storyfolio\\ndescription: Use when someone wants a personal portfolio site made from their profile, resume, LinkedIn or GitHub, especially one with 3D, scroll-driven animation or a story, or says their portfolio looks generic, templated or AI-made.\\n---\\n\\n# Storyfolio\\n\\nMakes one kind of portfolio site: one long scroll that tells one story, carried by one object in 3D that is taken from the person's own work.\\n\\nThis version plans the site and does not build it. It ends when the person has said yes to a storyboard.\\n\\n## Three stops\\n\\nBetween stops you work by yourself. At each stop the person decides one thing. You go on only when their answer is in the conversation and you have written it into the file.\\n\\n| Stop | First open | You put to the person | You go on when |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| 1. Read | `references/reading-a-profile.md` | What you found, as facts to confirm and questions to answer. Nothing else | They have answered, and `docs/story/facts.md` holds their answers |\\n| 2. Concept | `references/concept.md` | Three concepts, and which you would choose | They have picked one, or told you to pick, and `docs/story/concepts.md` says which |\\n| 3. Storyboard | `references/storyboard.md` | The script of the whole page | They have said yes to it |\\n\\n**Your first reply is the first stop, and no more than that.** People ask for the whole plan at once: the idea, the scroll, the colours. Do not give it yet, and say why in a sentence. A plan made now is made from your reading of a resume, and a resume leaves out exactly what a site must not get wrong: whose result a number was, what a title hides, who took a photograph. Once they have answered you will have a better idea, and it will not have to be taken apart.\\n\\nWhen the storyboard has its yes, say that building is not in this version, and bring `docs/story/handover.md` up to date.\\n\\n## Ask or decide\\n\\nAsk the person when a thing is:\\n\\n1. a fact only they know,\\n2. a claim that could embarrass them if it were wrong,\\n3. taste on what a visitor sees first: the concept, the look, the opening words,\\n4. anything that publishes, costs money, or shows another person or an employer's work.\\n\\nEverything else you decide. Write each decision into `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`: what you decided, why, and how to change it.\\n\\nIf the person will not answer, or tells you to decide everything, open `references/asking.md`.\\n\\n## What you keep\\n\\nIn the person's own folder, so that a later session can go on from the files alone:\\n\\n| File | Holds |\\n|---|---|\\n| `docs/story/facts.md` | The fact sheet, each fact with where it came from, and the person's answers |\\n| `docs/story/concepts.md` | The three concepts, which was picked, and why |\\n| `docs/story/storyboard.md` | The script |\\n| `docs/story/decided-for-you.md` | What you decided without asking |\\n| `docs/story/handover.md` | What exists, what the person has said, what is next |\\n\\n## What holds from the first stop on\\n\\n- **Nothing about the person is invented.** You know that a number, an employer, a title and a quote are facts. So is every small thing a sentence says on its way: what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used, which came first, why, how a thing was left, what it taught them. That sounds like writing, and it is a claim. Before handing over any reply or file, check each claim against the fact sheet, including introductory summaries, working titles and labels on the object's faces. Read the supporting line and its unresolved questions, not just its reference. It must establish the whole claim: a topic attached to one item does not establish the topic of another. Wording that depends on an unanswered question stays out of the introduction and the planned page, even if copied from a profile. Remove it or list it as a question to confirm.\\n- **A number is used as the person confirmed it,** with what it measures and whose result it is.\\n- **What is someone else's is asked about before it is planned for:** a photograph a photographer took, a friend's drawing, a quote, an employer's screens, a story with a patient or a client in it.\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n{\"type\":\"item.started\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_3\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc 'if [ -f docs/story/handover.md ]; then cat docs/story/handover.md; fi'\",\"aggregated_output\":\"\",\"exit_code\":null,\"status\":\"in_progress\"}}\n{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_3\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc 'if [ -f docs/story/handover.md ]; then cat docs/story/handover.md; fi'\",\"aggregated_output\":\"# Stop 4: local spine for appearance review\\n\\n## Person's words and current gate\\n\\nOn 11 October 2026 the user said yes to the derivative `storyboard.md` and\\nfictional `confirmations.md`, explicitly authorized building beyond the\\nStoryfolio skill's planning-only ending, and asked: “First build the spine:\\nthe opening, a representative middle chapter and the ending, in two or\\nthree looks for the same approved object. Let me scroll the working result\\nand choose a look before completing the rest.” Everything stays local.\\n\\nNo concept selection was restarted. Instrument paper\\nuses `?look=dark`; Review sheet uses `?look=review`. The switch preserves\\nscroll, fragment and other query parameters. The palette lives in\\n`content/looks.ts`; formations and face drawings live beside it.\\n\\nServer-rendered English text contains the approved opening definition,\\nAda's contribution, diagram limits and closing answer with projection,\\n72-hour run and unfinished qualification limits. The two local explanatory\\nSVGs are shown and linked, with their recorded alternative text. Email and\\ndownloadable corrected HTML CV are available in the header, opening and\\nclose. A local missing-page view has Home and Email Ada links.\\n\\nStatic modes use readable single-column text and large diagrams. At\\n767 CSS pixels or less, and with reduced motion at every width, the dynamic\\nscene never mounts. No JavaScript, no WebGL or renderer failure keeps the\\nspine text, diagrams and links. The current spine has three beats; the\\ncomplete seven-beat static contract becomes applicable when stop 5 is built.\\n\\nEngine changes are limited to the static-mode gate, optional bounded face\\naspect ratios for legible wide row textures, and explicit check-matrix\\nstatic-mode declarations. Optional starter extras and piece-overlay links\\nare not used by this spine. Existing engine defaults remain for other\\nbundles. System sans-serif and monospace fonts require no external service.\\n\\n## Environment and validation\\n\\nActual inspection found a supplied Next.js 16.3.8 starter and locked\\npackages, not a prior user portfolio. Node is v22.22.1. `npm ci` hit a\\nblocked registry request; `npm ci --offline` successfully installed all\\n392 locked packages from the available cache. file.\\n---\\n\\nThe `page` file allows you to define UI that is **unique** to a route. You can create a page by default exporting a component from the file:\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\nexport default function Page({\\n  params,\\n  searchParams,\\n}: {\\n  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>\\n  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>\\n}) {\\n  return <h1>My Page</h1>\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/blog/[slug]/page.js\\\" switcher\\nexport default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {\\n  return <h1>My Page</h1>\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Good to know\\n\\n- The `.js`, `.jsx`, or `.tsx` file extensions can be used for `page`.\\n- A `page` is always the **leaf** of the route subtree.\\n- A `page` file is required to make a route segment **publicly accessible**.\\n- Pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components) by default, but can be set to a [Client Component](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client).\\n- In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `page.js` is the innermost file convention. It is wrapped by `loading.js` (Suspense boundary), `error.js` (error boundary), `template.js`, and `layout.js` in the same segment.\\n\\n## Reference\\n\\n### Props\\n\\n#### `params` (optional)\\n\\nA promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) from the root segment down to that page.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({\\n  params,\\n}: {\\n  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>\\n}) {\\n  const { slug } = await params\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/shop/[slug]/page.js\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({ params }) {\\n  const { slug } = await params\\n}\\n```\\n\\n| Example Route                        | URL         | `params`                                |\\n| ------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |\\n| `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`            | `/shop/1`   | `Promise<{ slug: '1' }>`                |\\n| `app/shop/[category]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ category: '1', item: '2' }>` |\\n| `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`         | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`         |\\n\\n- Since the `params` prop is a promise, you must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.\\n  - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.\\n\\n#### `searchParams` (optional)\\n\\nA promise that resolves to an object containing the [search parameters](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters) of the current URL. For example:\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/shop/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({\\n  searchParams,\\n}: {\\n  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>\\n}) {\\n  const filters = (await searchParams).filters\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/shop/page.js\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({ searchParams }) {\\n  const filters = (await searchParams).filters\\n}\\n```\\n\\nClient Component **pages** can also access `searchParams` using React’s [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) hook:\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/shop/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\n'use client'\\nimport { use } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function Page({\\n  searchParams,\\n}: {\\n  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>\\n}) {\\n  const filters = use(searchParams).filters\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/page.jsx\\\" switcher\\n'use client'\\nimport { use } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function Page({ searchParams }) {\\n  const filters = use(searchParams).filters\\n}\\n```\\n\\n| Example URL     | `searchParams`                |\\n| --------------- | ----------------------------- |\\n| `/shop?a=1`     | `Promise<{ a: '1' }>`         |\\n| `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `Promise<{ a: '1', b: '2' }>` |\\n| `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `Promise<{ a: ['1', '2'] }>`  |\\n\\n- Since the `searchParams` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.\\n  - In version 14 and earlier, `searchParams` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.\\n- `searchParams` is a **[Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis)** whose values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it will opt the page into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)** at request time.\\n- With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), where you access `searchParams` in the component tree determines how much of the page can be prerendered. See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell).\\n- `searchParams` is a plain JavaScript object, not a `URLSearchParams` instance.\\n\\n### Page Props Helper\\n\\nYou can type pages with `PageProps` to get strongly typed `params` and `searchParams` from the route literal. `PageProps` is a globally available helper.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx\\\"\\nexport default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) {\\n  const { slug } = await props.params\\n  const query = await props.searchParams\\n  return <h1>Blog Post: {slug}</h1>\\n}\\n```\\n\\n> **Good to know**\\n>\\n> - Using a literal route (e.g. `'/blog/[slug]'`) enables autocomplete and strict keys for `params`.\\n> - Static routes resolve `params` to `{}`.\\n> - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build`, or with `next typegen`.\\n> - After type generation, the `PageProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\n### Displaying content based on `params`\\n\\nUsing [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes), you can display or fetch specific content for the page based on the `params` prop.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({\\n  params,\\n}: {\\n  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>\\n}) {\\n  const { slug } = await params\\n  return <h1>Blog Post: {slug}</h1>\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/blog/[slug]/page.js\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({ params }) {\\n  const { slug } = await params\\n  return <h1>Blog Post: {slug}</h1>\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Handling filtering with `searchParams`\\n\\nYou can use the `searchParams` prop to handle filtering, pagination, or sorting based on the query string of the URL.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/shop/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({\\n  searchParams,\\n}: {\\n  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>\\n}) {\\n  const { page = '1', sort = 'asc', query = '' } = await searchParams\\n\\n  return (\\n    <div>\\n      <h1>Product Listing</h1>\\n      <p>Search query: {query}</p>\\n      <p>Current page: {page}</p>\\n      <p>Sort order: {sort}</p>\\n    </div>\\n  )\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/shop/page.js\\\" switcher\\nexport default async function Page({ searchParams }) {\\n  const { page = '1', sort = 'asc', query = '' } = await searchParams\\n\\n  return (\\n    <div>\\n      <h1>Product Listing</h1>\\n      <p>Search query: {query}</p>\\n      <p>Current page: {page}</p>\\n      <p>Sort order: {sort}</p>\\n    </div>\\n  )\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Reading `searchParams` and `params` in Client Components\\n\\nTo use `searchParams` and `params` in a Client Component (which cannot be `async`), you can use React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to read the promise:\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/page.tsx\\\" switcher\\n'use client'\\n\\nimport { use } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function Page({\\n  params,\\n  searchParams,\\n}: {\\n  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>\\n  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>\\n}) {\\n  const { slug } = use(params)\\n  const { query } = use(searchParams)\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```js filename=\\\"app/page.js\\\" switcher\\n'use client'\\n\\nimport { use } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {\\n  const { slug } = use(params)\\n  const { query } = use(searchParams)\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Version History\\n\\n| Version      | Changes                                                                                                          |\\n| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\n| `v15.0.0-RC` | `params` and `searchParams` are now promises. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. |\\n| `v13.0.0`    | `page` introduced.                                                                                               |\\n---\\ntitle: Server and Client Components\\ndescription: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.\\nrelated:\\n  title: Next Steps\\n  description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.\\n  links:\\n    - app/api-reference/directives/use-client\\n    - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary\\n---\\n\\nBy default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.\\n\\nThis page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.\\n\\n> **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).\\n\\n## When to use Server and Client Components?\\n\\nThe client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.\\n\\nUse **Client Components** when you need:\\n\\n- [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.\\n- [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.\\n- Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `navigator.geolocation`, etc.\\n- [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).\\n\\nUse **Server Components** when you need:\\n\\n- Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.\\n- Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.\\n- Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.\\n- Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.\\n\\nFor example, the `<Page>` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `<LikeButton>` which handles client-side interactivity.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/[id]/page.tsx\\\" highlight={1,17} switcher\\nimport LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'\\nimport { getPost } from '@/lib/data'\\n\\nexport default async function Page({\\n  params,\\n}: {\\n  params: Promise<{ id: string }>\\n}) {\\n  const { id } = await params\\n  const post = await getPost(id)\\n\\n  return (\\n    <div>\\n      <main>\\n        <h1>{post.title}</h1>\\n        {/* ... */}\\n        <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />\\n      </main>\\n    </div>\\n  )\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/[id]/page.js\\\" highlight={1,13} switcher\\nimport LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'\\nimport { getPost } from '@/lib/data'\\n\\nexport default async function Page({ params }) {\\n  const { id } = await params\\n  const post = await getPost(id)\\n\\n  return (\\n    <div>\\n      <main>\\n        <h1>{post.title}</h1>\\n        {/* ... */}\\n        <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />\\n      </main>\\n    </div>\\n  )\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/ui/like-button.tsx\\\" highlight={1} switcher\\n'use client'\\n\\nimport { useState } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function LikeButton({ likes }: { likes: number }) {\\n  // ...\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/ui/like-button.js\\\" highlight={1} switcher\\n'use client'\\n\\nimport { useState } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function LikeButton({ likes }) {\\n  // ...\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## How do Server and Client Components work in Next.js?\\n\\n### On the server\\n\\nOn the server, Next.js uses React's APIs to orchestrate rendering. The rendering work is split into chunks, by individual route segments ([layouts and pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages)), including [parallel route slots](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) whether or not they are displayed:\\n\\n- **Server Components** are rendered into a special data format called the React Server Component Payload (RSC Payload).\\n- **Client Components** and the RSC Payload are used to [prerender](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) HTML.\\n\\n> **What is the React Server Component Payload (RSC)?**\\n>\\n> The RSC Payload is a compact, serialized representation of the rendered React Server Components tree. It's used by React on the client to update the browser's DOM. The RSC Payload contains:\\n>\\n> - The rendered result of Server Components\\n> - Placeholders for where Client Components should be rendered and references to their JavaScript files\\n> - Any props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component\\n\\n### On the client (first load)\\n\\nThen, on the client:\\n\\n1. **HTML** is used to immediately show a fast non-interactive preview of the route to the user.\\n2. **RSC Payload** is used to reconcile the Client and Server Component trees.\\n3. **JavaScript** is used to hydrate Client Components and make the application interactive.\\n\\n> **What is hydration?**\\n>\\n> Hydration is React's process for attaching [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events) to the DOM, to make the static HTML interactive.\\n\\n### Subsequent Navigations\\n\\nOn subsequent navigations:\\n\\n- The **RSC Payload** is prefetched and cached for instant navigation.\\n- **Client Components** are rendered entirely on the client, without the server-rendered HTML.\\n\\n## Examples\\n\\n### Using Client Components\\n\\nYou can create a Client Component by adding the [`\\\"use client\\\"`](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) directive at the top of the file, above your imports.\\n\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/ui/counter.tsx\\\" highlight={1} switcher\\n'use client'\\n\\nimport { useState } from 'react'\\n\\nexport default function Counter() {\\n  const [count, setCount] = useState(0)\\n\\n  return (\\n    <div>\\n      <p>{count} likes</p>\\n      <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Click me</button>\\n    </div>\\n  )\\n}\\n```\\n\\n\",\"exit_code\":0,\"status\":\"completed\"}}\n{\"type\":\"item.started\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_16\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc \\\"cat >       "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/README.md",
      "sha256": "b8b972ecd5a6492e26630483ff9f1c61823f8ca6a19df3943b78ac8c359df4e2",
      "bytes": 8174,
      "text": "# Storyfolio engine\n\nA starting project for one scroll, one story and one family of 3D pieces.\nThe supplied page is a plain test story, not a person's portfolio.\n\nTaken from V3 at `163b8ceb302b7b4e5beeff8f1161f4cdc7663b15` and made\nindependent of that site's content, paper shapes and assets. The source\nproject is unchanged. Storyfolio's engine and generated SVGs are MIT licensed.\n\n## Start\n\nUse Node 22.18 or later with native TypeScript support. Scaffold this folder\nwith `node <installed-skill>/scripts/scaffold.mjs <site-folder>`. Existing\n`docs/story/` files are kept; any conflicting engine path aborts the copy.\nThen, in the new site folder:\n\n```bash\nnpm ci\nnpm run browsers\nnpm run dev\n```\n\nOpen the local address printed by Next.js. Append `?look=dark` to choose a\nlook and `?fps` to show the frame meter. The appearance switch preserves\nother query parameters, the fragment and the current scroll position.\nRead the frame meter on a real phone; software rendering in a headless\nbrowser does not measure phone performance.\n\nNever install dependencies inside an installed skill. The copied project\nbelongs to the person, has its own lockfile, and does not depend on the\nskill after scaffolding. System fonts make builds independent of remote\nfont services. Add licensed local files with `next/font/local` if needed;\nthe scene starts without waiting for them and redraws faces when fonts load.\n\n## From storyboard to content\n\n`lib/story/` contains pure, tested calculations. `components/story/` owns\nthe browser and scene. The person's story belongs in `content/`:\n\n| File | Storyboard input |\n|---|---|\n| `story.ts` | Chapter IDs, names, roles, beat IDs and screen heights; one fixed piece count |\n| `formations.ts` | A rest formation for every beat; optional `within` formation reached as its rest is scrolled |\n| `faces.ts` | Pictures or canvas drawing functions for a beat and piece |\n| `copy.ts` | Metadata, language, labels and complete HTML text |\n| `looks.ts` | Ground, text and surface colors, lights and matte/no floor |\n| `extras.ts` | Lazy imports of chapter-specific shapes, each in its own error boundary |\n| `links.ts` | Ordinary HTML links over a named piece at a named beat |\n| `checks.json` | Optional checks of capabilities this fixture exercises |\n\nUse `as const satisfies StoryDef` for the story and\n`satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>` for formations. `checkStory`\nalso rejects invalid IDs, heights, piece counts and face references at\nruntime. A formation contains one position, rotation and size per piece,\nplus framing. `layouts.ts` supplies stack, fan, ring, grid, row and seeded\nscatter; `measure` bounds their rotated faces. Depth, a custom shape's\nextent and a whole formation's turn can require extra framing room.\n\nThe HTML in `app/page.tsx` follows the same beat order using `Chapter` and\n`Beat`. A `Beat` can carry a static `fallback` image or diagram. Keep one\n`h1`, stable chapter heading IDs and every factual claim in HTML. The check\nscript verifies the rendered beat IDs against the content contract.\n\nThe bundle type is in `components/story/types.ts`. Import a bundle inside a\nclient component, as `content/experience.tsx` does, and pass server-rendered\nHTML as children. Bundles contain drawing functions and component loaders,\nso cannot be serialized across a server/client prop boundary.\n\nA custom `Piece` component receives its index, face material and look.\nBuild it at unit width/height centered at the origin. Its parent group gets\nthe formation's position, rotation and width/height scale each frame. Keep\nmaterials present from the first frame. Extras receive the shared frame,\nlook, reduced-motion flag and control store and mount only near their\nchapter. Their shapes are children of the formation group.\n\nUse `useExtraFrame` from `components/story/extra-frame.tsx` for an extra's\nframe callback. It receives the same state, delta and optional XR frame as\nReact Three Fiber's `useFrame`. A synchronous exception disables that\ncallback immediately and unmounts its owning extra, leaving the core scene,\nother extras and HTML running. Each extra also has a React boundary for\nrender failures and rejected lazy imports. For example:\n\n```tsx\nuseExtraFrame(() => {\n  if (line.current) line.current.visible = frameRef.current.from === 1;\n});\n```\n\n`content/extras/middle-line.tsx` uses this hook. A raw third-party `useFrame`\ncallback, timer, event handler or rejected asynchronous task does not pass\nthrough this guard. Handle failures at those boundaries explicitly;\nwrapping a component in a React boundary does not catch them.\n\nFor caption controls, use `useControl` or `useControls` from\n`components/story/controls.tsx` in a client component. Real controls remain\nHTML. The canvas takes no pointer events. Overlay links are hidden and\nremoved from keyboard navigation outside their beat; supply the same\ndestination in the text for fallback access.\n\nFor a sketch, add a client component importing its own bundle and HTML to\n`content/sketches/index.ts`. Its key becomes `/sketch/<id>`. The initial\nregistry is empty and unknown keys return 404.\n\n## Check\n\n```bash\nnpm test\nnpm run typecheck\nnpm run lint\nnpm run check\n```\n\n`check` builds, starts its own production server on a free local port,\nruns the browser matrix and stops only that process group. It writes a\nmanifest, logs, reports and screenshots under `checks/<timestamp>/` and\nreturns a failure exit code for failed checks. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`\nselects an optional shared browser cache. `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE` is an optional\noverride; normally the installed local package provides the browser tool.\n\nThe matrix checks both looks at wide, short and phone sizes, reduced\nmotion, no WebGL and no JavaScript. Optional plain-story probes exercise\nkeyboard access and failed chapter loading. Context loss checks the HTML\nfallback. Wide captures include the beginning, middle and end of each\nbeat's rest; reduced-motion captures also check that a stationary scene\nstays still. Open every screenshot for overlap, clipping, legibility and\nframing. Automatic passes do not replace visual review.\n\nFor a focused investigation use `npm run check -- --only=light-phone`.\n`--skip-build` checks a previously built app and is diagnostic only.\nNeither establishes a fresh full acceptance run. `scripts/shoot.mjs`\ndocuments individual screenshots, blocked requests, look switching,\noverflow and shader checks.\n\nNo JavaScript leaves the server-rendered text. No WebGL or a failed scene\nleaves ordinary text and any beat's static image. Reduced motion cuts\nbetween poses, including within-beat formations, without idle movement.\nThe scene pauses offscreen, caps sharpness on touch devices and steps down\nquality when measured frames stay slow.\n\n## Ada Mensah: seven-beat local draft\n\nThis project continues the supplied spine with all six chapters and seven\nbeats, using the same six narrative rows. Bench paper is the selected look. Start with\n`NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npm run dev`, then scroll Bench paper (default),\nInstrument paper (`?look=dark`) and Review sheet (`?look=review`). The opening and closing surrounding copy await the user's choice before\nthe finishing pass; see `docs/story/copy-choices.md`. See `docs/story/handover.md`\nand `docs/story/review.md` for decisions and check evidence.\n\nThis fixture uses static HTML and supplied diagrams at widths up to 767px\nand under reduced motion. `content/checks.json` declares those checks. The\nsupplemental production check (retaining its original filename) is `node scripts/check-spine.mjs`; it checks\nthat those modes fetch no scene chunk, plus deep links, assets and contact\nlinks. Run it after the fresh production build from `npm run check`.\n\nThe sandbox's empty `.git` placeholder is read-only. Local commits use the\nproject's `.storyfolio-git` directory instead:\n`git --git-dir=.storyfolio-git --work-tree=. log --oneline`.\n\nFor environments that limit the lifetime of one command, `npm run check --\n--jobs=3 --wait=1000` runs the same full production matrix in independent\nbrowser batches, preserving its reports and exit status. The default\nremains sequential. This does not measure device performance.\n"
    },

      "text": "@import \"tailwindcss\";\n@import \"../components/story/story.css\";\n:root { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \"Segoe UI\", sans-serif; }\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nbody { margin: 0; }\na { color: inherit; }\nbutton, select { font: inherit; }\nhtml { scroll-behavior: auto; }\n.story { --font-story-display: system-ui, sans-serif; }\n.site-header { position: absolute; pointer-events: auto; }\n.wordmark { font: 600 1rem ui-monospace, monospace; text-decoration: none; }\n.wordmark span { font-size: .7rem; font-weight: 400; }\n.header-contact { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1.8rem; font-size: .75rem; }\n.header-contact .contact-links { margin: 0; gap: 1.8rem; font-size: .75rem; }\n.contact-links { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1.8rem; margin-top: 1.4rem; font-size: .9rem; }\n.contact-links a { text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--story-accent); padding-block: .5rem; }\n.file-type { font: .6rem ui-monospace, monospace; color: var(--story-faint); margin-left: .4rem; }\n.chapter-nav { position: absolute; top: 6.5rem; left: 3.5vw; z-index: 5; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1.2rem; font: .7rem ui-monospace, monospace; pointer-events: auto; }\n.chapter-nav a { text-decoration: none; }\n.chapter-nav span { color: var(--story-faint); }\n.story-bar { top: 8.5rem; height: calc(100lvh - 8.5rem); margin-bottom: calc(-100lvh + 8.5rem); padding-inline: 3.5vw; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-bar { top: 8.5rem; }\n.story-caption { padding: 3rem 5vw; }\n.story-caption-text { max-width: min(38vw, 34rem); }\n.story-title { font-size: clamp(2.2rem, 4.8vw, 5rem); font-weight: 550; letter-spacing: -.055em; line-height: 1.05; }\n.opening-question { font-size: clamp(1.2rem, 1.8vw, 1.65rem); line-height: 1.3; max-width: 26rem; margin: 1.2rem 0; letter-spacing: -.025em; }\n.story-body { font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.6; }\n.story-note { font-size: .85rem; line-height: 1.55; }\n.project-label { font: .7rem ui-monospace, monospace; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .04em; color: var(--story-accent); margin-top: 1.3rem; }\n.diagram-preview { margin: 1.5rem 0 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6.5rem 1fr; column-gap: 1rem; align-items: center; padding-top: 1rem; border-top: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--story-faint), transparent 55%); }\n.diagram-preview img { grid-row: 1 / 3; width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 2px; }\n.diagram-preview figcaption { font-size: .7rem; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--story-faint); }\n.diagram-preview a { font-size: .7rem; padding-block: .6rem; text-underline-offset: .25rem; }\n.story-rail { right: 2vw; }\n.story-rail a { font-size: .65rem; }\n.back-link { display: inline-block; font-size: .75rem; margin-top: 1.5rem; text-underline-offset: .3rem; }\n.site-footer { position: relative; padding: 1.5rem 3.5vw; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; border-top: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--story-faint), transparent 60%); font: .7rem ui-monospace, monospace; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] { padding-top: 14rem; padding-bottom: 0; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption-text { max-width: 45rem; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption { padding: 3rem max(5vw, calc((100vw - 55rem)/2)); }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-beat { border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--story-faint), transparent 70%); }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .diagram-preview { display: block; max-width: 32rem; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .diagram-preview img { width: 100%; margin-bottom: 1rem; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .diagram-preview figcaption { font-size: .85rem; }\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .diagram-preview a { display: inline-block; font-size: .85rem; }\n.missing-page { min-height: 100vh; padding: 15vh 10vw; background: #f2efe6; color: #282b29; }\n@media (max-width: 767px) {\n  .site-header { padding: 1.2rem; align-items: flex-start; }\n  .wordmark span { display: block; margin-top: .4rem; font-size: .6rem; }\n  .header-contact { display: block; }\n  .header-contact .contact-links { display: block; }\n  .header-contact .contact-links a { display: block; padding: .4rem 0; }\n  .header-contact > a { display: inline-block; margin-top: .6rem; }\n  .chapter-nav { top: 9rem; left: 1.2rem; right: 1.2rem; gap: 1rem; }\n  .chapter-nav span { width: 100%; }\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-bar { top: 15rem; padding: 0 1.2rem; justify-content: flex-start; }\n  .story-look-switch { flex-wrap: wrap; border-radius: .3rem; }\n  .story-look-switch button { padding: .5rem .6rem; font-size: .7rem; border-radius: .2rem; }\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] { padding-top: 20rem; }\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption { padding: 2.5rem 1.2rem; }\n  .story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-caption-text { max-width: 100%; }\n  .story-title { font-size: 2.8rem; }\n  .site-footer { padding: 1.5rem 1.2rem; flex-direction: column; }\n}\n/* Static content starts below the header; absolute navigation belongs to the story root. */\n.story[data-scene=\"off\"] .story-content { position: static; }\n/* Keep the appearance control above the rows on shorter desktop screens. */\n.story[data-scene=\"on\"] .story-bar { top: 5rem; height: calc(100lvh - 5rem); margin-bottom: calc(-100lvh + 5rem); }\n\n.surrounding-copy { font-size: .9rem; line-height: 1.55; margin-top: 1rem; }\n.evidence-limit { font: .75rem/1.5 ui-monospace, monospace; border-left: 2px solid var(--story-accent); padding-left: .8rem; margin-top: 1.4rem; }\n.diagram-prominent { grid-template-columns: 11rem 1fr; }\n@media (min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1100px) { .chapter-nav { max-width: 70%; gap: .7rem 1rem; } }\n"

      "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/app/page.tsx",
      "sha256": "88ed24917f7f90532d6c034b3f9e8273e9742bc517aa3d79ebde71adca43cd6e",
      "bytes": 3779,
      "text": "import { Chapter, Beat, Kicker, Title, Body, Note } from \"@/components/story/chapter\";\nimport { Experience } from \"@/content/experience\";\nimport { story } from \"@/content/story\";\nimport { copy } from \"@/content/copy\";\nconst contact = <div className=\"contact-links\"><a href=\"mailto:ada@example.com\">Email Ada <span aria-hidden=\"true\">↗</span></a><a href=\"/ada-mensah-cv.html\" download>Download CV <span className=\"file-type\">HTML ↓</span></a></div>;\nfunction Diagram({ fixture = false, prominent = false }: { fixture?: boolean; prominent?: boolean }) {\n  return <figure className={`diagram-preview${prominent ? \" diagram-prominent\" : \"\"}`}>\n    {/* Supplied local drawings have intrinsic dimensions and need no optimizer. */}\n    {/* eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element */}\n    <img src={fixture ? \"/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg\" : \"/assets/power-states.svg\"} width=\"720\" height=\"620\" alt={fixture ? \"Explanatory bring-up diagram linking firmware command, a generic board, the fixture and a bench observation. It contains no circuit detail.\" : \"Explanatory diagram: Sleep leads to Measure, then Transmit, then back to Sleep. No durations or measured current values are shown.\"} />\n    <figcaption>{fixture ? \"Explanatory schematic, not a photograph or a circuit diagram.\" : \"Explanatory schematic, not a measured trace or a firmware specification.\"}</figcaption>\n    <a href={fixture ? \"/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg\" : \"/assets/power-states.svg\"}>{fixture ? \"View fixture schematic\" : \"View power-state schematic\"} <span aria-hidden=\"true\">↗</span></a>\n  </figure>;\n}\nexport default function Home() {\n  return <main id=\"content\"><a className=\"story-skip\" href=\"#scope\">Skip to content</a><Experience>\n    <header className=\"site-header\"><a className=\"wordmark\" href=\"#scope\">AM<span> / STATE BY STATE</span></a><div className=\"header-contact\">{contact}<a href=\"#review\">Skip to contact</a></div></header>\n    <nav className=\"chapter-nav\" aria-label=\"Chapters\">{story.chapters.map(chapter => <a key={chapter.id} href={`#${chapter.id}`}>{String(chapter.number).padStart(2, \"0\")} {chapter.name}</a>)}</nav>\n    {story.chapters.map((chapter, index) => <Chapter key={chapter.id} id={chapter.id}>\n      {chapter.beats.map((beat, beatIndex) => { const words = copy.beats[beat.id]; return <Beat key={beat.id} story={story} id={beat.id}>\n        <Kicker number={chapter.number}>{chapter.name}</Kicker>\n        <Title id={beatIndex === 0 ? `${chapter.id}-title` : `${beat.id}-title`} as={index === 0 ? \"h1\" : beatIndex === 0 ? \"h2\" : \"h3\"}>{words.title}</Title>\n        {beat.id === \"scope.opening\" && <><p className=\"opening-question\">How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?</p><p className=\"surrounding-copy\">{copy.opening}</p></>}\n        <Body>{words.body}</Body><Note>{words.note}</Note>\n        {beat.id === \"scope.opening\" && <>{contact}<Diagram fixture /></>}\n        {beat.id === \"transition.diagram\" && <Diagram />}\n        {beat.id === \"observation.fixture\" && <Diagram fixture prominent />}\n        {beat.id === \"observation.evidence\" && <><Note>The longest run was 72 hours.</Note><Note>One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.</Note><p className=\"evidence-limit\">The 72-hour run does not validate the two-year projection.</p></>}\n        {beat.id === \"review.close\" && <><p className=\"surrounding-copy\">{copy.closing}</p><Note>The longest run was 72 hours.</Note><Note>One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.</Note>{contact}<a className=\"back-link\" href=\"#scope\">Back to Scope ↑</a></>}\n      </Beat>; })}\n    </Chapter>)}\n    <footer className=\"site-footer\">Ada Mensah · Firmware and the bench <span>State by state / Mosslink</span></footer>\n  </Experience></main>;\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/content/copy.ts",
      "sha256": "36b0c3190fd4bb8a6ade430bd15c3ea3b525c5108feda90161ca748866b15731",
      "bytes": 2558,
      "text": "export const copy = {\n  lang: \"en\",\n  metadata: {\n    title: \"Ada Mensah — Firmware and the bench\",\n    description: \"Firmware, power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture: Ada Mensah's contribution to Mosslink, with the evidence limits visible.\",\n    openGraph: { title: \"Ada Mensah — Firmware and the bench\", description: \"How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?\", images: [\"/assets/share-card.svg\"] },\n  },\n  railLabel: \"Chapters\", lookLabel: \"Appearance\", fpsLabel: \"Frames per second\",\n  opening: \"On Mosslink, an environmental sensor, my work spans firmware, power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture.\",\n  closing: \"Read the firmware contribution alongside the bench evidence and its limits.\",\n  beats: {\n    \"scope.opening\": { title: \"Ada Mensah\", body: \"Firmware is code that controls a physical device.\", note: \"I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture.\" },\n    \"responsibilities.split\": { title: \"Who made what\", body: \"I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture.\", note: \"A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end.\" },\n    \"state.table\": { title: \"Scheduling power states\", body: \"State tables, timing diagrams and current traces are daily working documents.\", note: \"Power-state scheduling was part of my contribution to Mosslink. These six narrative rows do not reproduce its firmware entries.\" },\n    \"observation.fixture\": { title: \"Checking basic operation\", body: \"Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation.\", note: \"I built the bring-up fixture. The drawing below explains the relationships between a firmware command, a generic board, the fixture and a bench observation.\" },\n    \"observation.evidence\": { title: \"What the bench supports\", body: \"Forty engineering samples were assembled. Six were tested on the bench. None went to customers.\", note: \"Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle.\" },\n    \"transition.diagram\": { title: \"Reading transitions\", body: \"Sleep → Measure → Transmit → Sleep. This teaching loop explains a transition between states.\", note: \"Explanatory schematic, not a measured trace or a firmware specification.\" },\n    \"review.close\": { title: \"Code beside evidence\", body: \"I connect firmware decisions to bench observations through power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture, while keeping the evidence limits visible.\", note: \"Two years is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle.\" },\n  },\n};\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/content/faces.ts",
      "sha256": "f6a2e566867c7d2f8f9a670a62b5307e4dac59adc6b73c1729a19c02b8f3db0a",
      "bytes": 2420,
      "text": "import type { FaceDef } from \"@/components/story/types\";\nimport { story, type BeatId } from \"./story\";\nconst table = [\"Scope / Firmware\", \"Responsibilities / Ada + colleague\", \"State / Power scheduling\", \"Transition / Teaching diagram\", \"Observation / Bench evidence\", \"Review / Evidence limits\"];\nconst labels: Record<BeatId, readonly string[]> = {\n  \"scope.opening\": table,\n  \"responsibilities.split\": [\"Ada / Firmware\", \"Ada / Power scheduling\", \"Ada / Bring-up fixture\", \"Colleague / PCB\", \"Colleague / Analogue front end\", \"Colleague / Circuitry\"],\n  \"state.table\": [\"Working document / State table\", \"Working document / Timing diagram\", \"Working document / Current trace\", \"Ada / Power scheduling\", \"Illustration / Narrative rows\", \"Actual firmware entries / Not shown\"],\n  \"transition.diagram\": [\"Sleep\", \"→ Measure\", \"Measure\", \"→ Transmit\", \"Transmit\", \"→ Sleep\"],\n  \"observation.fixture\": [\"Bring-up / Basic operation\", \"Teaching diagram / Firmware command\", \"Teaching diagram / Generic board\", \"Teaching diagram / Fixture\", \"Teaching diagram / Bench observation\", \"Limit / No circuit detail\"],\n  \"observation.evidence\": [\"Assembled / 40 engineering samples\", \"Bench tested / 6 samples\", \"Customers / None\", \"Projected / 2 years\", \"Longest run / 72 hours\", \"Full qualification / Unfinished\"],\n  \"review.close\": table,\n};\nexport const faces: FaceDef[] = story.chapters.flatMap(chapter => chapter.beats.flatMap(beat => Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, piece) => {\n  const aspect = beat.id === \"transition.diagram\" ? 2/.42 : beat.id === \"responsibilities.split\" ? 2.3/.46 : 3.65/.46;\n  return {\n    id: `${beat.id}-${piece}`, beat: beat.id, piece, aspect,\n    draw(ctx, width, height, look) {\n      const printedHeight = 1000/aspect;\n      ctx.scale(width/1000, height/printedHeight);\n      width = 1000; height = printedHeight;\n      ctx.fillStyle = look.surface.color; ctx.fillRect(0,0,width,height);\n      ctx.strokeStyle = look.faint; ctx.lineWidth = 1;\n      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(width*.13,0); ctx.lineTo(width*.13,height); ctx.moveTo(0,height*.93); ctx.lineTo(width,height*.93); ctx.stroke();\n      ctx.fillStyle = look.accent; ctx.font = `${height*.24}px monospace`; ctx.fillText(String(piece+1).padStart(2,\"0\"),width*.035,height*.58);\n      ctx.fillStyle = look.ink; ctx.font = `${height*.27}px system-ui`; ctx.fillText(labels[beat.id][piece],width*.17,height*.58, width*.79);\n    },\n  };\n})));\n"

      "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/content/formations.ts",
      "sha256": "79c1dedace0dd297aca6aa044249eacd62c0ffd5cde7123c47ee27679579f90f",

      "text": "import { blankFormation, type BeatFormation, type Formation, type Pose } from \"../lib/story/formation.ts\";\nimport { measure } from \"../lib/story/layouts.ts\";\nimport { story, type BeatId } from \"./story.ts\";\nfunction formation(pieces: Pose[], turn: [number, number] = [-.08, -.16]): Formation {\n  const bounds = measure(pieces);\n  return { ...blankFormation(story.pieces), pieces, span: bounds.span * 1.2, rise: bounds.rise * 1.05, anchor: [.45, .02], turn, near: 5, floor: -4 };\n}\nfunction table(depth: number): Pose[] {\n  return Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => ({ position: [0, (2.5-i)*.53, i*depth], rotation: [0,0,0], size: [3.65,.46] }));\n}\nconst loop: Pose[] = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => {\n  const p = [[-1.15,1.15],[1.15,1.15],[0,-1.05]][Math.floor(i/2)];\n  return { position: [p[0],p[1]-(i%2)*.48,0], rotation: [0,0,0], size: [2,.42] };\n});\nconst responsibilities: Pose[] = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => ({\n  position: [i < 3 ? -1.25 : 1.25, (1-i%3)*.62, i < 3 ? .04 : 0],\n  rotation: [0,0,0], size: [2.3,.46],\n}));\nconst bench: Pose[] = table(.025).map((pose, i) => ({ ...pose,\n  position: [0, (2.5-i)*.56, (i%2)*.06], rotation: [-.06,0,0],\n}));\nexport const formations = {\n  \"scope.opening\": { rest: formation(table(0)), within: formation(table(.045)) },\n  \"responsibilities.split\": { rest: formation(responsibilities, [0,-.08]) },\n  \"state.table\": { rest: formation(table(0), [0,0]) },\n  \"observation.fixture\": { rest: formation(bench, [-.16,-.1]) },\n  \"observation.evidence\": { rest: formation(table(0), [0,0]) },\n  \"transition.diagram\": { rest: formation(loop, [0,-.08]) },\n  \"review.close\": { rest: formation(table(.045)), within: formation(table(0)) },\n} satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>;\n"
    },

      "text": "# Spine review — ready for the person's look choice\n\n11 October 2026. This is stop 4, not approval of the completed site.\n\nThe local working spine contains Ada Mensah, Reading transitions and Code\nbeside evidence, carried by the same six row cards in all three looks.\nUse the appearance switch to compare Bench paper, Instrument paper and\nReview sheet while scrolling. No choice has yet been received.\n\n## Checks performed\n\n| Command / inspection | Result |\n|---|---|\n| `npm ci` | Registry request blocked; installation recovered with `npm ci --offline` (392 locked packages) |\n| `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/storyfolio-browser-cache npm run browsers` | Passed |\n| `npm test` | 131 passed, 0 failed |\n| `npm run typecheck` | Passed |\n| `npm run lint` | Passed |\n| `npm run check -- --jobs=3 --wait=1000` with supplied browser cache and libraries | Fresh production build; full matrix, 18/18 passed |\n| `node scripts/check-spine.mjs checks/2026-10-11T01-55-22-591Z/supplemental` with the same browser environment | Static chunk loading, desktop navigation/deep link, keyboard reachability, supplied assets, email/CV attributes and missing-page checks passed |\n| Visual inspection | All 93 matrix screenshots opened through labelled contact sheets; representative original desktop and phone images also opened. Supplemental screenshots opened separately. |\n\nProduction evidence: `checks/2026-10-11T01-55-22-591Z/`. Its manifest is\ncomplete and reports no browser problems. The tracked compact record is\n`check-results.json`; logs, individual PNGs and labelled contact sheets\nremain locally under that check folder. Previous runs were stopped for\nvisual corrections or terminated before completion; they are not acceptance\nruns. The final checker still defaults to sequential execution; optional\nbatching preserved the entire matrix within the environment's runtime limit.\n\n## Observations\n\nThe desktop table stays framed beside the prose, separates into Sleep,\nMeasure and Transmit teaching pairs, then returns to its row formation.\nThe third appearance changes the palette to cool paper and blue annotations;\nit keeps the same object and factual labels. All looks keep readable text\nand labelled explanatory drawings. The short-desktop switch is above the\nrows. Phone header, chapter links, switch and opening now have separate\nspace. Large static diagrams are readable without the canvas.\n\nPhone and reduced-motion contexts each mounted zero canvases and requested\nzero identified scene chunks. Desktop mounted one canvas and fetched that\nchunk. Direct arrival at `#transition` and navigation to `#review` settled\nwith the matching active scene chapter. Switching appearances preserved the\nfragment, other query parameters and scroll in the matrix. Context loss\nremoved the scene and retained the HTML presentation.\n\nInitial screenshot inspection found stretched/blurred row text, a static\nheader overlap, and a short-screen control overlap. These were corrected\nbefore the final complete run. Static snapshots can start partway through a\nsection because the engine samples scroll rests; the full text remains in\nordinary document flow and is reachable by scrolling.\n\n## Scope and limits\n\nThe remaining four beats and their core sentences are intentionally deferred\nuntil the person chooses a look. The full seven-beat content contract has\nnot yet been completed or approved. No fictional response is counted as\nreal scrolling review. No real phone performance, mail delivery, legal\nadequacy, deployment or external social-card compatibility is established.\nThe corrected CV is HTML. The two diagrams are explanatory SVGs, not\nphotographs, circuitry, measured traces or specifications.\n\n## Awaiting\n\nThe person's choice: Bench paper, Instrument paper or Review sheet. After\nthat, continue stop 5 without restarting the concept: add Responsibilities,\nState and both Observation beats, keep all eleven confirmed sentences and\nsix chapter links, and offer the requested surrounding-copy choices.\n"

      "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/scripts/check-spine.mjs",
      "sha256": "17f887e864571b2c157d912e66488aaa0ed324cabc310c5c4f404cf893bff69a",
      "bytes": 6182,
      "text": "// Seven-beat draft supplemental checks. Use a freshly built app after npm run check.\nimport { chromium } from 'playwright-core';\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { createServer } from 'node:net';\nimport { readFile, readdir, mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nconst output = process.argv[2] ?? 'checks/spine-supplemental';\nawait mkdir(output, { recursive: true });\nconst socket = createServer();\nawait new Promise(ok => socket.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', ok));\nconst port = socket.address().port;\nawait new Promise(ok => socket.close(ok));\nconst server = spawn(process.execPath, ['node_modules/next/dist/bin/next', 'start', '--hostname', '127.0.0.1', '--port', String(port)], { env: { ...process.env, NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1' }, stdio: 'ignore' });\nconst base = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;\nlet browser;\nconst results = [];\nconst core = (await readFile('docs/story/confirmations.md', 'utf8')).split('\\n').filter(line => /^\\d+\\. /.test(line)).map(line => line.replace(/^\\d+\\. /, ''));\nassert.equal(core.length, 11);\nconst chapterIds = ['scope', 'responsibilities', 'state', 'transition', 'observation', 'review'];\nconst beatIds = ['scope.opening', 'responsibilities.split', 'state.table', 'transition.diagram', 'observation.fixture', 'observation.evidence', 'review.close'];\ntry {\n  for (let i=0; i<100; i++) {\n    try { if ((await fetch(base)).ok) break; } catch {}\n    await new Promise(ok => setTimeout(ok, 100));\n  }\n  const sceneChunks = [];\n  for (const file of await readdir('.next/static/chunks')) {\n    if (file.endsWith('.js') && /story-face-v1|WebGLRenderer/.test(await readFile(`.next/static/chunks/${file}`, 'utf8'))) sceneChunks.push(file);\n  }\n  assert.ok(sceneChunks.length, 'identify actual scene chunk');\n  browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox', '--use-angle=swiftshader', '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader', '--ignore-gpu-blocklist'] });\n  for (const mode of ['phone', 'reduced', 'desktop', 'no-js', 'no-webgl']) {\n    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: mode==='phone' ? { width:390, height:844 } : { width:1440, height:900 }, javaScriptEnabled: mode !== 'no-js', reducedMotion: mode==='reduced' ? 'reduce' : 'no-preference' });\n    if (mode === 'no-webgl') await context.addInitScript(() => {\n      const original = HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext;\n      HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext = function(kind, ...args) {\n        if (/webgl/i.test(kind)) return null;\n        return original.call(this, kind, ...args);\n      };\n    });\n    const page = await context.newPage(); const requests=[];\n    page.on('request', request => requests.push(request.url()));\n    await page.goto(`${base}/`, { waitUntil:'networkidle' });\n    await page.screenshot({ path:`${output}/${mode}-initial.png` });\n    await page.goto(`${base}/#transition`, { waitUntil:'networkidle' }); await page.waitForTimeout(2500);\n    const canvas = await page.locator('canvas').count();\n    const requestedScene = requests.filter(url => sceneChunks.some(chunk => url.endsWith('/'+chunk)));\n    if (mode==='desktop') {\n      assert.equal(canvas,1); assert.ok(requestedScene.length);\n      assert.equal(await page.locator('.story-rail a[aria-current]').getAttribute('href'), '#transition');\n      await page.screenshot({ path:`${output}/desktop-deep-transition.png` });\n      await page.locator('.story-rail a[href=\"#review\"]').click(); await page.waitForTimeout(2500);\n      assert.equal(await page.locator('.story-rail a[aria-current]').getAttribute('href'),'#review');\n      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');\n      assert.ok(await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName === 'A' || document.activeElement?.tagName === 'BUTTON'));\n    } else {\n      assert.equal(canvas,0);\n      if (mode !== 'no-webgl') assert.deepEqual(requestedScene,[]);\n    }\n    assert.deepEqual(await page.locator('[data-beat]').evaluateAll(nodes => nodes.map(node => node.dataset.beat)), beatIds);\n    assert.deepEqual(await page.locator('.chapter-nav a').evaluateAll(nodes => nodes.map(node => node.getAttribute('href'))), chapterIds.map(id => '#'+id));\n    for (const sentence of core) assert.ok(await page.getByText(sentence, { exact: true }).count(), `missing approved sentence: ${sentence}`);\n    const headingIds = await page.locator('h1,h2,h3').evaluateAll(nodes => nodes.map(node => node.id));\n    assert.equal(new Set(headingIds).size, 7);\n    for (const chapter of chapterIds) {\n      await page.goto(`${base}/#${chapter}`, { waitUntil:'networkidle' });\n      await page.waitForTimeout(mode === 'desktop' ? 1500 : 100);\n      if (mode === 'desktop') assert.equal(await page.locator('.story-rail a[aria-current]').getAttribute('href'), '#'+chapter);\n    }\n    await page.locator('[data-beat=\"observation.evidence\"]').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();\n    await page.waitForTimeout(1500);\n    await page.screenshot({ path:`${output}/${mode}-evidence.png` });\n    assert.ok(await page.getByText(core[6], { exact: true }).first().isVisible());\n    assert.equal(await page.locator('h1').count(),1);\n    for (const path of ['/assets/power-states.svg','/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg','/assets/share-card.svg','/icon.svg','/ada-mensah-cv.html']) assert.equal((await context.request.get(base+path)).status(),200);\n    assert.equal(await page.locator('a[download]').count(),3);\n    assert.equal(await page.locator('a[href=\"mailto:ada@example.com\"]').count(),3);\n    assert.equal((await context.request.get(`${base}/missing-address`)).status(),404);\n    await page.goto(`${base}/missing-address`); assert.equal(await page.getByRole('link',{name:'Home',exact:true}).getAttribute('href'),'/');\n    assert.equal(await page.getByRole('link',{name:'Email Ada',exact:true}).getAttribute('href'),'mailto:ada@example.com');\n    results.push({mode,canvas,requestedScene,passed:true}); await context.close();\n  }\n  await writeFile(`${output}/report.json`, JSON.stringify({ sceneChunks, results, limits:'Automated Chromium checks; no real phone, mail delivery, publication or social-platform validation.' },null,2)+'\\n');\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(results));\n} finally { await browser?.close(); server.kill('SIGTERM'); }\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "run/turns/01/snapshot/files/scripts/review-screenshots.mjs",
      "sha256": "e76915a45e0b7157102c921922142c27acfe94e217fe19aa4eb4cbd8c6daba6e",
      "bytes": 1467,
      "text": "// Local contact sheets for visual inspection of every check screenshot.\nimport { chromium } from 'playwright-core';\nimport { readdir, readFile, mkdir } from 'node:fs/promises';\nconst run = process.argv[2];\nif (!run) throw new Error('Usage: node scripts/review-screenshots.mjs checks/<run>');\nconst browser = await chromium.launch({args:['--no-sandbox']});\nconst page = await browser.newPage({viewport:{width:1600,height:1000}, deviceScaleFactor:1});\nawait mkdir(`${run}/visual-sheets`,{recursive:true});\nfor(const dir of await readdir(run,{withFileTypes:true})) {\n  if(!dir.isDirectory() || dir.name==='visual-sheets') continue;\n  const files=(await readdir(`${run}/${dir.name}`)).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.png')).sort();\n  if(!files.length)continue;\n  let html='<style>body{margin:0;background:#d9d9d9;font:12px monospace}main{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:8px;padding:8px}figure{margin:0;background:white;padding:4px}img{width:100%;height:235px;object-fit:contain}figcaption{padding:5px}</style><main>';\n  for(const file of files)html+=`<figure><img src=\"data:image/png;base64,${(await readFile(`${run}/${dir.name}/${file}`)).toString('base64')}\"><figcaption>${dir.name}/${file}</figcaption></figure>`;\n  await page.setContent(html+'</main>');\n  await page.locator('img').evaluateAll(imgs=>Promise.all(imgs.map(img=>img.decode())));\n  await page.screenshot({path:`${run}/visual-sheets/${dir.name}.png`,fullPage:true});\n}\nawait browser.close();\n"
    },
